title: A whole-life fatigue crack growth rate prediction method based on active learning and physics-informed loss
abstract: Whole-life fatigue crack growth presents a critical challenge in structural integrity assessment, particularly under complex loading conditions. To address the limitations of standard physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in capturing the temporal dynamics of fatigue crack growth, this study proposes an active learning-based physics-informed recurrent neural network (AC-PI-RNN). Specifically, a recurrent neural network (RNN) is integrated with a fully connected network, where dynamic features (stress intensity factor range) and static features (stress ratio, load amplitude, and pre-strain) are fused at the RNN input layer to provide comprehensive loading information. To optimize sample selection under data-limited conditions, a query-by-committee active learning strategy is employed. Furthermore, a modified Jones physical model is embedded into the network's loss function to enforce adherence to the underlying physics of fatigue crack growth. Comprehensive evaluations validate the efficacy of the proposed framework, demonstrating enhanced predictive fidelity, robust generalization, and improved physical consistency. A comparative analysis reveals that the AC-PI-RNN significantly outperforms traditional RNN and PINN models, showing a distinct advantage in capturing the complete trajectory of whole-life crack propagation with high precision. The proposed framework provides an effective and interpretable approach for whole-life fatigue crack growth rate prediction under complex loading conditions.

title: Adversarial contrastive learning to augment deep knowledge tracing
abstract: Knowledge Tracing forecasts students’ future learning outcomes by analyzing historical interactions and modeling learning trajectories, which is essential for personalized learning on online education platforms. However, deep knowledge tracing methods face challenges due to data sparsity, which hinders their ability to differentiate between interactions and leads to overfitting. To address the challenge of data sparsity, this paper proposes a deep knowledge tracing approach that integrates an adversarial contrastive learning framework. This framework generates challenging adversarial samples and uses contrastive learning to refine the model’s discrimination accuracy, helping it learn subtle distinctions between sample categories and improving overall performance. Additionally, our approach incorporates a self-attention mechanism to integrate information from multiple knowledge points, further improving adversarial sample quality through enhanced question embeddings. Experimental results on various real-world educational datasets show that our method significantly outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy, particularly in datasets with different levels of sparsity, effectively mitigating overfitting. Furthermore, the adversarial contrastive learning framework not only improves the performance of individual models but also demonstrates scalability and flexibility, enabling integration and enhancement of numerous existing knowledge tracing models.

title: Anomaly detection of bamboo chopsticks based on cross-domain mixup augmentation and self-supervised learning
abstract: Aiming at the practical problem of visual detection of abnormal surface quality of disposable bamboo chopsticks in an industrial production environment, this paper proposes an application-oriented anomaly detection algorithm based on cross-domain mixup augmentation (CDMA) and self-supervised learning to improve the inspection quality of bamboo chopsticks in production. Firstly, a novel data augmentation algorithm is proposed, which combines cross-domain sample images unrelated to chopsticks images with normal sample images to generate pseudo-abnormal samples and drive model learning. Then, a self-supervised learning algorithm based on intra-class relevance retrieval and reconstruction constraints is proposed. This model reconstructs the normal input images and its associated intra-class image, and at the same time, adds regular term constraints to the pseudo-abnormal images, so that their reconstruction errors could not be lower than a limited value, so as to increase the discrimination with the normal samples. Finally, the maximum local error is used to generate anomaly scores for detection. The experimental results show that the detection accuracy and speed performance of the algorithm have reached an advanced level.

title: Fractal-guided multi-scale contrastive learning for robust liver tumor classification in ultrasound
abstract: Ultrasound-based liver lesion classification remains challenging because diagnostically relevant cues are often localized, structurally heterogeneous, and easily corrupted by speckle noise, boundary ambiguity, and acquisition variability. Existing deep learning methods mainly emphasize global image-level representations and may therefore be suboptimal for modeling lesion-relevant local morphology. We propose a structure-constrained multi-scale contrastive learning framework for liver ultrasound classification. During training, semantic-guided anchoring is used to identify informative local regions, within which positive samples are selected under joint constraints of semantic similarity, local statistical consistency, and fractal-based structural complexity. A multi-scale local positive mining strategy and multi-positive supervised contrastive objective are further introduced to capture lesion patterns across different spatial granularities and enhance class discrimination. Importantly, the framework requires no auxiliary annotations during inference and operates directly on full ultrasound images. Experiments on a private four-class liver ultrasound dataset and two public ultrasound datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over representative convolutional neural network-based, Transformer-based, self-supervised, and ultrasound-specific methods. On the private dataset, the proposed method achieved 97.27% accuracy, and maintained 91.15% accuracy on an independent external validation cohort. Ablation studies and interpretability analyses further show that the method improves both structural discriminability and lesion-focused attention. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and practically deployable solution for robust liver lesion classification in ultrasound imaging.

title: Enhancing air quality forecasting through homogeneous transfer learning: A novel approach for improved accuracy
abstract: Air pollution from various sources poses a significant threat to human health and the environment. Developing accurate air quality prediction models is crucial for effective environmental monitoring and public health management. Transfer learning has emerged as a promising approach to enhance such models by leveraging knowledge from related domains. This research paper explores the application of homogeneous transfer learning for building more efficient air quality prediction models. By adapting pre-trained models to new air quality datasets, transfer learning improves predictive accuracy, reduces training time, and addresses data scarcity issues. Meteorological and pollutant data from Trivandrum are collected to develop an Air Quality Prediction model. The knowledge from this prebuilt model is then utilized to construct an Air Quality Index (AQI) model for the Cochin region using the deep learning algorithms Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), where data availability is limited. Experimental evaluations on diverse datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of homogeneous transfer learning in enhancing air quality forecasting. The findings highlight the impact of transfer learning in creating robust air quality index models, aiding pollution control and mitigation strategies.

title: Solving ill-posed inverse heat conduction: Reconstruction of blast furnace inner wall temperature fields using a physics-informed diffusion model
abstract: The internal temperature field of a blast furnace, vital for steelmaking, impacts energy use, emissions, and smelting costs, ensuring operational stability. Direct measurement of inner wall temperatures is infeasible due to the furnace’s enclosed, dusty, high-temperature, and high-pressure environment. Current approaches thus rely on sparse outer wall thermocouple measurements to reconstruct the internal temperature field via mathematical models. However, the large furnace volume coupled with limited outer wall data lead to a highly ill-posed inverse heat conduction problem, hindering accuracy and efficiency for industrial needs. To address this, we propose Diffusion-PINN, a Diffusion-Physics-Informed Neural Networks, which transforms the temperature field inversion into a diffusion-based generation process for temperature distribution maps. For the inverse heat conduction problem, the diffusion model is designed to fit the joint distribution of inner and outer wall temperature fields, directly generating coupled temperature distributions to circumvent the multi-solution issue of inverse problems. To address sparse measurement points and enhance solution accuracy, physical heat transfer information is embedded as conditional constraints in the diffusion process, progressively narrowing the constraint range during training. A dynamic loss-pulling algorithm is further proposed to enhance both solution accuracy and training speed. For the challenge of large spatial scales, the computationally intensive inversion process is reduced to a highly parallelizable map generation task, enabling rapid reconstruction of large-scale temperature fields. Simulations demonstrate that this method effectively addresses ill-posed inverse heat conduction problems. When applied to blast furnace smelting, it achieves the accuracy and efficiency required for industrial applications, offering substantial practical value.

title: A Dual-Encoder Convolutional Neural Networks–Frequency Transformer framework with bidirectional attention for precise brain tumor segmentation
abstract: Brain tumors present significant neurological challenges with high mortality rates, where early diagnosis based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is clinically vital but is hindered by labor-intensive manual segmentation. To overcome limitations in existing approaches, where convolutional neural networks (CNNs) struggle with global context dependencies and Transformers face computational inefficiency, we propose a dual-branched framework called bifurcated fusion dual-encoder convolutional neural networks –frequency Transformer (BiF-DTNet). The BiF-DTNet employs a dual-encoder architecture, where the CNN encoder captures local features. In contrast, the frequency-domain vision Transformer (FViT) encoder efficiently models global context through fast Fourier transform and self-attention. The model incorporates bidirectional spatial-channel attention (BISC) blocks for effective multi-scale feature fusion, enhancing segmentation accuracy. While BiF-DTNet performs feature encoding on two-dimensional (2D) axial slices for computational efficiency, the model reconstructs the final segmentation in a volumetric manner, enabling precise and coherent three-dimensional (3D) tumor prediction. Evaluated on the brain tumor segmentation (BraTS) 2020 and BraTS 2021 benchmarks, BiF-DTNet achieves Dice scores of 80.42%/85.15%/91.34% (enhancing tumor (ET)/tumor core (TC)/whole tumor (WT)) on BraTS 2020 and 85.98%/91.25%/93.64% on BraTS 2021, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. These results conclusively demonstrate BiF-DTNet’s superiority in precise 3D tumor segmentation, particularly for irregular boundaries and small lesions, through its synergistic integration of local and global features.

title: Active learning driven materials discovery for low thermal conductivity rare-earth pyrochlore for thermal barrier coatings
abstract: High-Entropy/multicomponent rare-earth oxides (HECs and MCCs) show promise as alternative materials for thermal barrier coatings (TBC) with the ability to tailor properties based on the combination of rare-earth elements present. By enabling the substitution of scarce or supply-risk rare-earths with more readily available alternatives while maintaining comparable material performance, HECs and MCCs offer a valuable path towards alternative TBC material design. However, navigating this search space of compositionally complex materials is both time and resource intensive. In this study, an active learning (AL) framework was employed to identify HEC/MCC materials with a pyrochlore structure, with acceptable thermal conductivity (TC) for TBC applications. The AL framework was applied through a Bayesian optimisation (BO) strategy, coupled with a random forest surrogate model. TC was selected as the optimisation criterion as that is the most fundamental requirement of TBC materials. Over two iterations of the AL cycle, four compositions were generated and synthesised in the lab for experimental evaluation. The first iteration yielded two single-phase pyrochlores, ( La 0 . 29 Nd 0 . 36 Gd 0 . 36 ) 2 Zr 2 O 7 and ( La 0 . 333 Nd 0 . 26 Gd 0 . 15 Ho 0 . 15 Yb 0 . 111 ) 2 Zr 2 O 7 , with measured thermal conductivities of 2.03 and 1.90 W/mK, respectively. The surrogate model predicted a TC of 2.009 W/mK for both compositions, demonstrating its accuracy for completely new compositions. The second iteration compositions showed dual-phase when synthesised, highlighting the need to take into account phase formation in the AL framework.

title: Toward brain magnetic resonance imaging analysis intelligence: A review of federated learning and visual foundation models
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is central to brain research and clinical care. However, heterogeneity across scanners, acquisition protocols, and populations, together with privacy constraints, limits the reliability and scalability of the magnetic resonance imaging analysis. In this review, we use brain MRI analysis intelligence (BMI) to denote a layered and governance-aware framework. This framework integrates visual foundation models (VFMs) and federated learning (FL) through shared anatomical representations, lightweight center-local adaptation, and federated orchestration with provenance tracking, privacy budgets, and rollback mechanisms. This review (i) outlines brain magnetic resonance imaging fundamentals and major task categories; (ii) surveys federated learning as a practical route for multi-center collaboration without sharing raw data; and (iii) summarizes visual foundation model pretraining and fine-tuning methods for label-efficient and cross-contrast adaptation. Finally, we summarize three principles toward brain magnetic resonance imaging analysis intelligence: representation first, orchestration always, and measure what matters. Looking ahead, federated visual foundation models, domain adaptation, and governance-aware continual learning could further advance the analysis intelligence toward routinely audited clinical use.

title: Joint underwater image enhancement and multi-scale fish detection
abstract: Automatic fish detection in images plays a crucial role in marine biodiversity monitoring and environmental conservation. The advent of deep learning has significantly improved the results achievable in fish detection; however, underwater challenges such as scale variability, optical distortions, and color inconsistencies reveal some limitations of conventional deep learning-based detectors. To address these issues, we propose an improved fish detection model designed for underwater environments trained to perform joint underwater image enhancement and multi-scale fish detection. While incorporating structural enhancements for multi-scale robustness, such as a dedicated tiny object detection head and attention mechanisms, the core of our approach resides in the joint training of an underwater image enhancement module with the detector. We evaluate our method on two challenging test sets. The experimental results demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average precision between 0.84 and 0.89. Despite its superior accuracy, the proposed solution maintains a lightweight architecture with only 24 millions of parameters and ensures real-time processing capabilities (13 frames per second on edge hardware), highlighting its potential for effective deployment in marine research and autonomous fisheries monitoring. • YOLO-JUICE boosts small-object detection with an extra tiny-object head. • YOLO-JUICE preserves details without extra cost with a space to depth module. • YOLO-JUICE refines spatial and channel features with a spatial-channel attention. • YOLO-JUICE is jointly trained for image classification and enhancement.

title: Accurately modelling the resting-state functional connectivity with eigen-based connected-graph diffusion model
abstract: Understanding how functional dynamics emerge from the brain’s underlying structural architecture remains a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Conventional graph diffusion (GD) models are limited by sparse anatomical connectivity, leading to a failure to capture indirect connectivity and negatively correlated relationships. To overcome these challenges, we introduce hypergraphs and deep neural networks to enhance the representation of brain connectivity. Specifically, graphs and hypergraphs are integrated to construct a connected-graph, providing a comprehensive representation of inter-regional brain connectivity. The Fourier-induced deep neural network is employed to infer latent inter-regional relationships from structural connectivity by leveraging spectral features, effectively capturing both low- and high-frequency components. These deduced relationships are incorporated into the connected-graph, giving rise to a connected-graph diffusion (CD) model, which is further refined via eigen-decomposition to form an eigen-based connected-graph diffusion (ECD) model. Evaluated on 1012 subjects from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) S1200 release, the ECD model achieves a mean Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.7230 in functional connectivity (FC) prediction, outperforming the GD model (0.5513) and CD model (0.6518). The stability analysis demonstrates that the prediction of the ECD model is reliable. This work demonstrates that integrating biological mechanisms with machine learning methods can accurately model complex brain networks, with implications for neural signal processing, brain-inspired computing, and neuropsychiatric diagnosis.

title: Physics-informed neural network modeling for digital control of pneumatic systems with binary valve inputs and adaptive parameter identification
abstract: Accurate dynamic modeling of pneumatic actuation systems is crucial for design optimization and control stability. Traditional physics-based models struggle with accuracy and adaptability due to factors like gas compressibility, nonlinear friction, and varying operating conditions, while data-driven models often lack physical consistency and generalize poorly under extrapolated conditions. Although physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) effectively combine physical priors with data-driven learning, existing approaches focus primarily on systems with continuous control inputs, with limited attention given to digitally controlled pneumatic systems using binary on-off valve signals and hybrid dynamics. Furthermore, most PINN methods assume known physical parameters. This paper presents a PINN-based framework for digitally controlled pneumatic systems, directly using binary valve signals as inputs, embedding governing dynamics as soft constraints in the loss function, and introducing a physical-parameter encoder for key constants. An adaptive range-optimization mechanism is also introduced to identify difficult-to-calibrate parameters such as dead volume and friction. Validation of the approach on two pneumatic platforms demonstrates its superiority over purely data-driven feedforward neural networks (FNN) in predicting displacement and pressure, achieving R2 > 0.99 under supply pressure conditions outside the training set. These results confirm the model's accuracy, generalization, and adaptability across diverse operating conditions.

title: A novel Adaptive Loss Weighting–Gradient-Based Attention framework for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in flow simulation
abstract:
Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) provide a mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) by embedding physical laws directly into the training process, making them particularly attractive for complex engineering applications such as computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Despite their promise, conventional PINNs often struggle to enforce boundary conditions (BCs) accurately, resulting in suboptimal performance for challenging flow simulations.
This paper proposes a novel Adaptive Loss Weighting (ALW) scheme combined with a Gradient-Based Attention (GBA) mechanism to enhance boundary condition enforcement in PINNs. The ALW strategy dynamically rebalances the contributions of the PDE residual and boundary loss terms during training, while the GBA mechanism selectively emphasizes boundary collocation points associated with large gradients, thereby guiding the optimization process more effectively.

title: Uncertainty-aware precipitation nowcasting with diffusion model simulating precipitation evolution processes
abstract: Precipitation nowcasting is a critical field of meteorology research. Current methods fail to fully account for uncertainties in nowcasting, leading to issues such as ambiguity, omission, and localized bias. This paper introduces a conditional diffusion model to mitigate uncertainty by modeling the probability distribution of spatio-temporal evolution features of precipitation. Based on the continuity equation of precipitation evolution, an evolution feature autoencoder decouples the precipitation evolution process into motion fields and precipitation intensity residuals through two distinct encoding pathways. The diffusion model based on U-shaped architecture with spatio-temporal attention mechanism, simulates precipitation evolution conditioned on evolution features. Accurate nowcasting is achieved by decoding the generated spatio-temporal evolution features into precipitation. Extensive experiments on two real-world precipitation datasets demonstrate that the proposed method mitigates uncertainties in nowcasting, particularly for high-intensity precipitation, achieving improvements of at least 10.9% in Critical Success Index (CSI) and and 9.8% in Heidecker Skill Score (HSS) over state-of-the-art methods.

title: Surrogate modeling of inductance in axial active magnetic bearings using data-driven and physics-informed neural networks
abstract: In active magnetic bearing (AMB) systems, accurate modeling of nonlinear electromagnetic effects is essential for high-fidelity simulation and control design. Conventional approaches rely on either analytical approximations, which are often too simplified to capture the full nonlinear behavior, or on finite element method (FEM)-based lookup tables, which require computationally expensive interpolation and exhibit poor generalization in sparsely sampled regions. This motivates efficient surrogate modeling approaches that preserve FEM-level accuracy while enabling scalable, continuous evaluation. This paper proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach for inductance modeling in axial AMBs, combining data-driven learning with electromagnetic circuit physics. Two architectures are developed for comparison: a purely data-driven NN and a PINN. The main novelty of this work is a physics-informed learning formulation in which the actuator voltage equation as an ordinary differential equation (ODE) constraint, is embedded into the PINN loss function, enabling consistent enforcement of the nonlinear electrical dynamics and the coupled dependence of inductance on airgap position and coil current. The trained models are validated under open- and closed-loop conditions with position and inner current control, followed by offline experimental verification using data collected from a real AMB setup. Comparative analysis with a data-driven NN, Polynomial Regression, and Gaussian Process Regression surrogate models demonstrates that incorporating physics-based constraints into the loss function improves model accuracy and consistency, particularly in sparsely sampled regions. The proposed PINN thus provides a physics-consistent and computationally efficient surrogate model for axial AMB systems, replacing conventional FEM-based lookup tables.

title: When control meets large language models: From words to dynamics
abstract: While large language models (LLMs) are transforming engineering and technology through enhanced control capabilities and decision support, they are simultaneously evolving into complex dynamical systems whose behavior must be regulated. This duality highlights a reciprocal connection in which prompts support control system design while control theory helps shape prompts to achieve specific goals efficiently. In this study, we frame this emerging interconnection of LLM and control as a bidirectional continuum, from prompt design to system dynamics. First, we investigate how LLMs can advance the field of control in two distinct capacities: directly, by assisting in the design and synthesis of controllers, and indirectly, by augmenting research workflows. Second, we examine how control concepts help LLMs steer their trajectories away from undesired meanings, improving reachability and alignment via input optimization, parameter editing, and activation-level interventions. Third, we look into deeper integrations by treating LLMs as dynamic systems within a state-space framework, where their internal representations are closely linked to external control loops. Finally, we identify key challenges and outline future research directions to understand LLM behavior and develop interpretable and controllable LLMs that are as trustworthy and robust as their electromechanical counterparts, thereby ensuring they continue to support and safeguard society.

title: Improving fire and smoke detection with ghost convolutions, Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Networks, and image enhancement
abstract: Wildfire monitoring is an important application of artificial intelligence for reducing ecological, economic, and human losses through earlier and more reliable fire and smoke detection. Conventional methods, such as satellite surveillance, often suffer from limited coverage, delayed response times, and reduced effectiveness in complex outdoor environments. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly the You Only Look Once (YOLO) family of object detectors, have shown strong potential for real-time wildfire detection. However, these models still face challenges related to computational overhead and reduced robustness under low-contrast conditions. This paper introduces You Only Look Once version 11 small with Ghost Neck and Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (YOLOv11s-GN+BIFPN), an enhanced object detection framework based on the small variant of YOLOv11. Ghost Neck (GN) modules are incorporated into both the backbone and neck of the network to reduce feature redundancy and improve computational efficiency. A Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BIFPN) is further integrated at the Pyramid Level 4 (P4) stage to strengthen multi-scale feature fusion, enabling more effective detection of fire and smoke objects across different sizes. In addition, several image enhancement techniques are systematically evaluated, including contrast stretching (CS), histogram equalization (HE), dual gamma correction (DGC), contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE), and their hybrid combinations. Experiments on the Fire and Smoke dataset containing 11,667 images show that CLAHE+CS preprocessing combined with YOLOv11s-GN+BIFPN achieves the best performance, reaching 89.50% mean Average Precision (mAP). This result surpasses the baseline YOLOv11 and recent state-of-the-art models.

title: GeoFusion: A hybrid convolutional neural network-transformer model for boreal peatland classification
abstract: The generation of high-resolution boreal peatland maps through the integration of multi-source remote sensing data provides critical support for greenhouse gas inventories and environmental management. In this study, we propose GeoFusion, a pixel-wise peatland classification architecture that leverages open-access radar imagery from Sentinel-1 and optical imagery from Sentinel-2. GeoFusion combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for hierarchical local feature extraction with vision transformers (ViTs) for modeling long-range dependencies, enabling effective fusion of spectral–textural and structural information. The architecture also incorporates data augmentation, multi-head self-attention, and dropout regularization to enhance robustness and mitigate overfitting. Performance was assessed at two classification levels: site type and fertility level, capturing both ecological diversity and functional characteristics of complex peatland ecosystems. Comparative experiments against well-known deep learning models and hybrid Transformer-based models were conducted across three ecologically distinct regions in Finland. The obtained results demonstrate that GeoFusion outperforms other models and achieves average accuracies of 79.25% and 72.68% for fertility-level and site-type predictions, respectively.

title: A comparative study on monthly precipitation forecasting using time-series foundation models in South Korea
abstract: In this study, four artificial intelligence-based time-series foundation models were evaluated: a generative pretrained transformer for time series (TimeGPT), Time Series Foundation Model (TimesFM), Chronos, and Moirai. These models were used to forecast monthly precipitation in four major cities in South Korea: Seoul, Daejeon, Daegu, and Busan. Because of increasing uncertainty in weather forecasts caused by climate change, the development of accurate and efficient prediction models is critical. Historical monthly precipitation data from the Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS), spanning 1985 to 2024, were partitioned into separate training and test sets. We applied a sliding-window approach for continuous model retraining and quantitatively evaluated the prediction accuracy against seasonal autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. The results highlight the complementary strengths of the time-series foundation models and LSTM baseline relative to the SARIMA benchmark. Moirai was effective in predicting intense, highly variable monsoon rainfall, whereas TimesFM provided stable skill during other, more predictable seasons and surpassed SARIMA in root mean square error (RMSE) for Seoul. The LSTM baseline underperformed in full-period error metrics, but reproduced peak and dry-month precipitation more accurately than the other models, underscoring a tradeoff between average accuracy and fidelity to extremes. SARIMA achieved the lowest full-period RMSE and mean absolute error for most city–lead time combinations. Overall, these findings suggest that combining time-series foundation models with traditional statistical and deep-learning forecasting methods can yield more balanced forecasting performance with lower full-period errors and better capture of extremes.

title: Identifying the post-pandemic determinants of low performing students in Latin America through interpretable Machine Learning methods
abstract: The high prevalence of students not achieving the basic competencies in Latin America is concerning. Even more so given the region’s deep structural inequalities and the larger post-pandemic regional learning losses. Within this scenario, this paper contributes to the identification of the determinants of bottom and low performers (below level 2) using recent advancements on explainable machine learning methods. In particular, relying on PISA 2022 data for 10 countries and using the Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis, I identify critical factors impacting on the student performance across low performers groups. I find that a student with the highest probability of being a not achiever speaks a minority language and had repeated, has no digital devices at home, comes from a poor family and works for payment half of the week, and the school he/she attends has wide disadvantages such as bad school climate, weak ICT infrastructure and poor teaching quality (only a third of teachers being certified). Regarding countries' estimates, I find quite homogeneous patterns as far as global average contribution of top ranked factors is concerned, with repetition at primary, household wealth, and educational ICT inputs being top ten ranked covariates in at least 8 out of the 10 total countries. The paper findings contribute to the broad literature on strategies to identify and to target those most left behind in Latin American education systems.

title: Uncertainty-aware dynamic graph contrastive learning for node classification and anomaly detection
abstract:
Dynamic graph contrastive learning methods commonly assume that nodes preserve stable structural roles over time. However, real-world networks often violate this assumption: nodes may change their connectivity patterns, reactivate after long inactivity, or undergo local structural reorganisation. Such heterogeneity not only weakens temporal consistency constraints but also causes volatile nodes to generate unreliable negative signals. This work shows that temporal contrasts vary substantially in reliability and should not be treated uniformly.

We introduce an uncertainty-aware dynamic graph contrastive learning framework driven by temporal contrast uncertainty, which quantifies the reliability of cross-temporal contrasts directly from the graph structure. Nodes with low temporal contrast uncertainty exhibit stable structural patterns, whereas nodes with high temporal contrast uncertainty indicate volatile evolution. Leveraging temporal contrast uncertainty, the proposed framework integrates three mechanisms: (1) adaptive temporal sampling, (2) uncertainty-weighted contrastive objectives, and (3) group-level prototype calibration to correct estimation bias. We theoretically show that temporal contrast uncertainty weighting yields a favourable trade-off with respect to the mutual information lower bound, while prototype calibration provides an upper bound for controlling temporal drift. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets for node classification and seven datasets (including two with real-world anomaly labels) for anomaly detection demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with pronounced improvements on datasets containing a high proportion of structurally volatile nodes.

title: Subgraph-based contrastive learning with distribution alignment for graph anomaly detection
abstract: Graph anomaly detection has become increasingly crucial for identifying suspicious patterns in complex networks, with broad applications in domains such as social network analysis, fraud detection and network security. Recent advances in graph contrastive learning (GCL) have demonstrated great potential for unsupervised anomaly detection by capturing discriminative representations from local subgraphs. However, existing GCL-based methods still face challenges in detecting subtle anomalies due to the inherent structural heterogeneity of real-world graphs. Furthermore, their reliance on rigid or stochastic subgraph sampling strategies limits their ability to capture fine-grained structural variations, thereby reducing detection sensitivity. To address these limitations, we propose a subgraph-based contrastive learning framework for graph anomaly detection, referred to as SubGAD. Specifically, SubGAD constructs informative subgraph views by integrating first- and second-order neighbors, thereby capturing richer contextual patterns without the bias of fixed-size sampling. It first performs node-to-subgraph contrastive learning to highlight local deviations, and then introduces the Graph Earth Mover’s Distance (G-EMD) to align subgraph representations across views, effectively quantifying structural and semantic discrepancies in a distribution-aware manner. Moreover, SubGAD mitigates positional bias through subgraph centering and performs kernel-based anomaly detection. Extensive experiments on seven real-world datasets demonstrate that SubGAD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving notable performance gains and confirming its effectiveness in detecting subtle anomalies in attributed graphs. Our source code is available at https://github.com/GNNteam/SubGAD.

title: Physics-informed belief rule base with high interpretability model for complex mechatronic system performance evaluation considering intermittent power
abstract: Intermittent power (IP) has become an important operational strategy for complex mechatronic systems (CMS) due to its energy-saving potential and dynamic adaptability. However, most existing performance evaluation models assume stable power supply and therefore fail to accurately capture the performance degradation of CMS under IP conditions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-informed belief rule base model with high interpretability for CMS performance evaluation under IP conditions, termed IPBRB-IP. An event-driven damage accumulation model for IP (DAM-IP) is first developed to calculate dynamic damage factors, through explicit embedding of physical knowledge. An interval belief rule base is then constructed, where the bounds of belief distributions are determined conservatively and aggressively using expert knowledge and limited data. Based on the calculated damage factors, the initial belief distributions are adaptively inferred, allowing accurate representation of the performance degradation trajectory of CMS. To further preserve interpretability, an interpretability-constrained optimization criterion is introduced to ensure cognitive consistency between physics-corrected expert understanding and model outputs. Finally, a CMS case study under IP conditions demonstrates the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed approach. From an artificial intelligence perspective, this work develops a physics-informed and interpretable belief rule base framework that integrates damage modeling and knowledge–data fusion for CMS performance evaluation under IP. From an engineering perspective, the proposed IPBRB-IP model provides a transparent and reliable tool for performance evaluation of CMS operating under IP conditions.

title: A novel extreme gradient boosting based adaptive genetic algorithm method for electro-thermal performance optimization of power integrated circuits
abstract: Effective thermal management for high-power-density integrated circuits faces significant challenges due to electrical and dimensional constraints in modern electronic systems. Existing design methods often treat thermal analysis as a post-layout verification step, lacking efficient co-optimization strategies. This paper proposes a co-optimization method that integrates data-driven modeling with an adaptive genetic algorithm. First, an electro-thermal coupling model generates a calibrated dataset, enabling the development of a high-precision chip temperature predictor using the extreme gradient boosting algorithm. The proposed model then optimizes printed circuit board layout parameters under simultaneous electrical and dimensional constraints. The integrated extreme gradient boosting based adaptive genetic algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional models, achieving an average temperature reduction of 2.92% over the standard genetic algorithm and 4.93% over Bayesian optimization. Subsequent simulations and experimental validations confirm the accuracy of steady-state temperature predictions. Experimental findings reveal that, across varying load conditions, the optimized samples exhibit an average target temperature reduction of 7.95%, with a maximum decrease of 8.54 °C. These results demonstrate its practical value of the proposed model, providing an optimization strategy for thermal design of high-power-density integrated circuits.

title: Hybrid fractional-order physics-informed neural network and reinforcement learning framework with blockchain for dynamic optimization of flux, fouling and heavy metal rejection in metal foam-enhanced direct contact membrane distillation systems
abstract: Heavy metal contamination in industrial wastewater requires sustainable remediation solutions. This study introduces a hybrid computational framework combining Fractional-Order Physics-Informed Neural Networks (FO-PINNs) for surrogate modeling, Reinforcement Learning (RL) for dynamic optimization, and blockchain for auditable logging, applied to Direct Contact Membrane Distillation (DCMD). Under CFD-verified simulation conditions over a 12-h cycle (1500 epochs), the framework predicts a mean permeate flux of 4.51 L/m^{2}.h, representing a 32% improvement compared to non-foam CFD baselines, and suggests a 68% reduction in fouling rate. Energy-intensity modeling, after subtracting computational overhead, indicates an approximate 15% net reduction in CO_{2} emissions under the simulated operating conditions. Blockchain provides auditable data tracking, while a GUI facilitates dynamic optimization. While experimental validation remains necessary, this approach demonstrates the feasibility of physics-informed adaptive control for DCMD and offers a foundation for scalable, low-carbon wastewater treatment.

title: Neural network-driven inverse design of a two-dimensional photonic crystal waveguide with a 90-degree bend for low-loss and broadband transmission in telecommunication bands
abstract: Optical communication systems require compact routing elements that maintain high transmission while minimizing bending loss. This study presents an artificial-intelligence-assisted inverse-design framework based on a multilayer perceptron neural network to optimize a two-dimensional photonic crystal waveguide incorporating a 90-degree bend for broadband telecommunication operation. First, three candidate bend configurations were evaluated using full-wave electromagnetic simulations, and the third configuration provided the best conventional performance, achieving a maximum bandwidth of 165.1 nm with a minimum transmission loss of 11.76 percent, including 73.1 nm within the original telecommunication band. Next, the multilayer perceptron neural network was trained on simulated samples incorporating waveguide operating conditions, enabling rapid prediction of improved geometric parameters. The waveguide predicted by the neural network was then re-simulated, demonstrating a 26.288 percent increase in bandwidth to 208.5 nm. In this case, the proposed waveguide completely covered the original telecommunications band and 50.6 nm of the telecommunications Extended-band. Across the entire operating bandwidth, transmission losses remained below 10 percent, and at the peak bandwidth, they were below 1.2 percent, representing an 89.8 percent reduction compared to the previous best case. These results show that neural network-based inverse design can efficiently identify parameter settings that substantially improve bandwidth and reduce loss in photonic crystal waveguide bends, providing a practical route toward data-driven design of photonic integrated circuits.

title: Physics-informed surrogate modeling for hydrogen production in plastic waste gasification
abstract: In this study, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework was proposed for predicting hydrogen production in the gasification of plastic waste by embedding kinetic- and equilibrium-based physical knowledge as soft constraints into the learning process. Three PINN variants—kinetic, equilibrium, and combined—were developed and compared with a conventional artificial neural network (ANN) under varying dataset ratios (1%, 10%, 50%, and 100%) to evaluate their performance in data-scarce environments. Although the ANN model exhibited substantial performance degradation with limited data, all PINN models maintained robust predictive accuracy (R^{2}, the coefficient of determination >0.99) and physically plausible behavior within the surrogate modeling scope, with the equilibrium model achieving the lowest error and the combined model showing the best overall balance. Gradient-based residual analysis also confirmed that the PINN results were consistent with expected thermodynamic and reaction trends, rather than strictly enforcing the governing physical laws. Although the models were trained on simulated data from a simplified single-unit process, they have demonstrated their effectiveness as a proof-of-concept for physics-guided surrogate modeling, providing a useful basis for future real-time optimization and control of hydrogen production systems.

title: Boundary Region Reinforcement Physics-Informed Neural Networks for solving partial differential equations
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a deep learning framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs). However, standard approaches often struggle to strictly enforce boundary conditions, limiting their computational accuracy, especially in complex multiphysics coupled systems. To address this challenge, we introduce Boundary Region Reinforcement Physics-Informed Neural Networks (BRR-PINNs), a novel framework designed to strengthen boundary constraint enforcement and significantly improve solution accuracy. The method converts non-Dirichlet conditions into exact Dirichlet boundaries using intermediate variables to reduce redundant loss terms, and applies a spatial reinforcement function to prioritize training near boundaries. We validate the effectiveness of BRR-PINNs on a two-dimensional axisymmetric thermo-elastic coupling problem, involving a circular ring subjected to both thermal and mechanical loads. Experimental results show that our method consistently outperforms several existing approaches, achieving approximately one order of magnitude improvement in accuracy.

title: Fragment target-based unsupervised transformer-enhanced deep image prior for selected-band hyperspectral image super-resolution
abstract: High-resolution hyperspectral images enable precise fragment detection, explosive residue analysis, and explosion-proof design. Owing to technical restrictions in hyperspectral sensor hardware, significant challenges exist in acquiring high-resolution hyperspectral images of small-sized fragments at a safe standoff distance. Hyperspectral image super-resolution (HISR) technology can compensate for the limitations of single-sensor imaging, enabling the simultaneous acquisition of spatial details and spectral information of fragments. However, most existing super-resolution networks are trained on simulated degraded image pairs, failing to account for the issue of spatial misalignment between heterogeneous sensors. Therefore, a mathematical observation model is developed to describe the physical degradation during the fusion of fragment low-resolution hyperspectral images and high-resolution Red-Green-Blue (RGB) images, considering the presence of spatial misalignment. Based on these models, we then propose a fragment target-based unsupervised transformer-enhanced deep image prior network (FT-UTDIP-Net) for selected-band HISR. The network comprises modules for image registration and blur kernel learning, initial image estimation generation, multi-scale feature progressive alignment, and super resolution hyperspectral image generation. The proposed method achieves promising fusion performance for HISR across both public and selected-band steel fragment datasets. Furthermore, downstream experiments demonstrate that the method significantly enhances fragment recognition performance. This study demonstrates feasibility for selected-band HISR of steel fragments under a controlled UAV acquisition setting.

title: Toward ahead prediction of molten pool penetration states in laser welding via physics-informed spatiotemporal learning
abstract: In laser welding, the penetration state is a critical factor affecting joint formation quality and service performance. However, during actual welding processes, the molten pool exhibits a delayed response to heat input, and the welding system inherently involves unavoidable delays, which significantly limit the effectiveness of traditional real-time monitoring and control methods. To address these issues, this research proposes a laser welding molten pool state ahead prediction method that integrates physics features based on dimensionless numbers, aiming to mitigate delay effects in the welding process and to provide predictive state information for intelligent welding process control. The proposed method exploits image sequences to characterize the dynamic behaviors of the molten pool and keyhole. By analyzing the thermal history characteristics of the welding process, a penetration state score model is introduced, providing a physical motivation for modeling temporal dependencies. On this basis, dimensionless number-based physics features are collaboratively integrated with image sequences, leading to the development of a physics-informed multi-scale temporal convolutional network (MSP-TCN). The proposed model is capable of learning the evolution patterns of the molten pool state across different welding scenarios in a more stable manner, thereby enabling ahead prediction of molten pool state sequences. Experimental validation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms purely image-driven models in terms of both prediction accuracy and generalization capability, providing an effective solution for delay compensation in laser welding processes.

title: Quantifying physics-informed causal pathways in flow-induced vibration heat transfer enhancement through spectral dynamics and mediation analysis
abstract: Most flow-induced vibration (FIV) studies rely on amplitude or correlations without quantifying causal paths. We introduce a physics-informed causal inference framework to explain heat transfer mechanisms. A directed acyclic graph was pre-specified from fluid–structure–thermal interaction principles and evaluated using mediation analysis of 120 high-fidelity simulations covering Re = 2300–7700, Ur = 5–15, and G = 0.4–1.2. The optimal spectral-response regime achieved a peak performance evaluation criterion (PEC) of 1.32 ± 0.03 (sampling error; combined uncertainty ±0.06), exceeding the energy-efficiency threshold of PEC = 1.0, while excessive structural stiffness reduced PEC by 18.3%. Three dominant causal pathways were statistically validated, with path coefficients of |β| = 0.25–0.38 (bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero) (p < 0.001). Compared with an amplitude-only benchmark, spectral features explained an additional 18.3% of performance variance and mediated 63–64% of the total causal effect from system parameters to performance, demonstrating that vibration quality is not a secondary descriptor but a primary causal determinant. Physically, high Spectral Purity enabled vortex–thermal phase locking with Δt/T = 0.12 ± 0.02, Harmonic Energy Ratio predicted regime transitions with 87% accuracy and a 6% false-positive rate, and high Modal Coherence directed 72% of vibrational energy into productive thermal mixing, compared with only 38% in low-coherence configurations. Bootstrap resampling confirmed that the identified causal pathways remained directionally consistent in more than 96% of resamples. The present framework lies not only in predicting enhanced heat transfer but also in explaining why it occurs, thereby shifting FIV thermal-system design from amplitude maximization toward spectral-quality optimization.

title: Attention-based graph neural operators for learning parametric response mappings in discrete structures
abstract:
Parametric analysis of discrete engineering structures requires repeated finite element simulations, leading to high computational cost in design exploration. Graph neural operators have emerged as a promising surrogate modeling framework for learning parametric solution mappings on graph-structured systems; however, existing approaches remain limited in effectively capturing long-range dependencies.

This study introduces an attention-based graph neural operator (AGNO) for learning parametric response mappings in discrete structural systems under variations in node-indexed features, particularly structural geometry (via nodal coordinates) and applied nodal loading. The proposed model integrates kernel-induced graph neural operator layers, which emulate operator learning through edge-conditioned message passing, with a permutation-invariant global attention mechanism acting on graph-indexed latent functions, resulting in a unified local–global operator architecture.

The key contribution lies in addressing the locality of graph neural operators in the context of discrete structural systems through this local–global operator architecture. This formulation enables effective modeling of nonlocal structural interactions while preserving topology-aware local behavior, and provides a principled operator-learning framework tailored to graph-based structural response problems.

The approach is evaluated on benchmark problems involving two- and three-dimensional trusses and frames, including mesh-refinement studies and scaling to larger structural systems. Results show that AGNO demonstrates strong performance compared to existing graph-based and operator-learning surrogate models across the considered benchmarks, achieving lower prediction errors and improved robustness with respect to discretization refinement and increasing geometric complexity, while maintaining comparable computational cost. These findings indicate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for parametric response prediction in discrete structural systems under the tested conditions.

title: A unified causality-enhanced separable physics-informed neural network for predicting beam and plate dynamics
abstract: A thorough understanding of the dynamic behavior of structural elements, such as beams, plates, and membranes, is crucial for reliable structural analysis. This behavior is typically governed by higher-order partial differential equations (PDEs), which accurately capture their spatiotemporal response. However, the presence of high-order differential operators and inherent high-frequency components, especially over large spatial domains, poses challenges for Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). To tackle this challenge, we propose a causality-informed Separable Physics-Informed Neural Network (SPINN) framework augmented with auxiliary variables (Causal Aux SPINN) to enhance the performance of PINNs in structural engineering applications. The proposed framework integrates three key components. First, the SPINN formulation decomposes the spatiotemporal solution into low-rank components, allowing efficient representation of high-dimensional dynamic fields with reduced computational cost. Second, the causality-informed loss function re-weights the training objective to respect the temporal evolution of structural dynamics and mitigate error accumulation over time. Third, the auxiliary-variable formulation introduces additional outputs for second-order fields, such as curvature-related quantities, enabling accurate enforcement of fourth-order differential operators without relying solely on successive differentiation of displacement fields. The proposed “Causal Aux SPINN” algorithm is evaluated on both forward and inverse benchmarks in structural dynamics, including Euler–Bernoulli and Timoshenko beams, membranes, and Kirchhoff–Love plates. Across all benchmarks, the Causal Aux SPINN method consistently reduces error and improves robustness, while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to the Baseline SPINN formulation. Overall, coupling causal weighting with auxiliary-variable learning is shown to provide an effective framework for structural engineering applications.

title: Applications of generative models in medical imaging:A review
abstract: Generative models have become a foundational technology for medical imaging, supporting image generation, enhancement, segmentation, registration, image-to-image translation, and anomaly detection. Despite the rapid growth of methodological work, the literature still lacks a unified comparative framework that helps practitioners decide between Generative Adversarial Networks, Variational Autoencoders, and diffusion models for specific medical-imaging tasks; existing surveys also provide limited treatment of validation strategies, dataset constraints, and ethical or clinical considerations. This survey reviews representative methods from each model family across six core tasks, covering anomaly detection, image-to-image translation, image generation, segmentation, denoising, and registration, consolidating them into a unified comparison spanning accuracy, computational cost, data requirements, robustness, uncertainty quantification, and practical deployment. We further compile commonly used benchmark datasets together with their scale, diversity, and known limitations, and we critically discuss validation strategies, model complexity and regularization, and ethical, clinical, and practical considerations. Our key findings are threefold. First, no single model family dominates across all tasks, as Generative Adversarial Networks remain leading for image-to-image translation and data augmentation, Variational Autoencoders are well-suited to reconstruction-based anomaly detection where their posterior provides native uncertainty estimates, and diffusion models currently offer the strongest results in image generation, segmentation, and denoising. Second, practical deployment metrics and external validation remain under-reported in the literature, which limits clinical translation. Third, domain shift, demographic bias, regulatory uncertainty, and reproducibility are open challenges shared across model families. We close with a conceptual taxonomy organized along the model-family by imaging-task axis and outline future research directions.

title: Multi-component Weather Prediction using Self-Supervised Multi-Fidelity Ensemble Learning with Model Explainability
abstract: Accurate weather prediction remains a persistent challenge due to the multi-component nature of atmospheric systems and the limitations of traditional forecasting models. This study presents an Artificial Intelligence (AI)–driven weather forecasting framework that integrates Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), self-supervised learning, ensemble learning, and explainable AI techniques. Particularly, we propose a Self-Supervised Multi-Fidelity Ensemble Learning (SSMFEL) model, which integrates low-, mid-, and high-fidelity long short-term memory architectures with regularization, dropout, and a decoder to extract meaningful patterns from unlabeled data. The proposed model achieved over 95% R-squared ( R 2 ) metric, coefficient of determination, for humidity and temperature prediction and more than 52% R 2 for wind speed and precipitation, significantly outperforming existing ML, DL, and transformer-based models. SSMFEL also demonstrated the 0.00018 Mean Squared Error (MSE) and 0.03489 root MSE across all components. Results from test statistic tests , sensitivity analysis, and fairness evaluation further confirmed the statistical superiority of the proposed approach. Model explainability analysis revealed that specific humidity is the most influential feature, while temperature and relative humidity contribute contextually. Theoretical analysis based on bias–variance reduction and generalization theory further supports the improved forecasting performance of the proposed method.

title: Reinforcement learning-enhanced barrier function super-twisting sliding mode control for bidirectional electric vehicle charging with superconducting magnetic energy storage
abstract: The fast development of electric vehicles is putting a strain on the possibility of having intelligent bidirectional charging infrastructures, which are capable of supporting vehicle to grid operation but are also able to handle renewable intermittency and rapid load swings. The current energy management and control policies of renewable-integrated charging stations frequently cannot be used to guarantee high power quality, real-time feasibility, and robust stability at the same time, especially when sophisticated storage technology is used. This paper develops a unified control and artificial intelligence solution to bidirectional electric vehicle charging which integrates superconducting magnetic energy storage with solar photovoltaic and wind generation. A barrier based super-twisting sliding mode controller is designed at the control level to impose safety requirements, enhance disturbance rejection, and reduce chattering with parameter uncertainty. Red Fox Optimization aims at optimizing controller gains with the view of improving dynamic performance. Bidirectional recurrent neural networks at the intelligence layer forecast renewable power, and a Deep Q-Network based reinforcement learning energy management system optimizes and determines the best power scheduling between the grid, renewable sources, electric vehicle battery and superconducting magnetic storage. In addition, performance of the proposed super-twisting sliding mode controller with enhanced barrier functionality is compared to a synergetic approach to control and confirmed in a high-fidelity hardware-in-the-loop experiment. High-fidelity simulations and experimental validation demonstrate improved charging efficiency, enhanced utilization of superconducting magnetic energy storage during fast transients, and reduced total harmonic distortion during transitions between grid-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-grid modes. The proposed framework offers a scalable and intelligent solution for renewable-aware bidirectional charging in sustainable transportation systems.

title: TDFormer: A novel triple decoupled transformer for accurate multi-step wind power forecasting
abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting (WPF) is crucial for ensuring the stable operation of power systems. Long-term effective forecasting can optimize wind power generation planning and reduce operational costs. Although deep learning advancements have significantly improved wind power forecasting accuracy, existing methods often struggle to effectively separate the complex relationships between variables, features, and time dimensions in multivariate time-series data, limiting their predictive performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel model, named Triple Decoupled Transformer (TDFormer), for multi-step wind power forecasting. The model incorporates a novel Triple Decoupled Attention (TDA) mechanism to independently decouple input data across three dimensions—variables, features, and time—enabling more efficient and precise feature extraction. TDFormer adopts an encoder-decoder architecture to integrate historical data from multiple variables and future time sequences, making it ideal for multi-step wind power forecasting. Extensive experiments conducted on real-world datasets from wind farms with varying capacities and geographical locations demonstrate that the proposed TDFormer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, especially in scenarios involving longer forecasting horizons. In addition, the model demonstrated excellent generalization ability and practical application potential in the transfer learning experiments, making it particularly suitable for newly established wind farms with limited data, and offering significant application value. The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/USTC-AI4EEE/TDFormer.

title: Deep learning framework for the diagnosis of systemic sclerosis using serum-derived microbial signatures
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare and severe autoimmune disease of unknown etiology, currently lacking effective treatment. Therefore, early diagnosis and timely intervention are critical for improving clinical outcomes. Accumulating evidence implicates the human microbiome as a key contributor to SSc pathogenesis, with distinct microbial alterations identified in patients. Given that circulating anti-microbial immunoglobulin M(IgM) antibodies reflect recent and systemic microbial perturbations across multiple organ systems, comprehensive profiling of serum IgM antibodies against diverse microbial species may offer a promising strategy for predicting early disease development through the identification of SSc-associated microbial signatures. However, predictive diagnostic models incorporating microbiome derived serological data in SSc have not yet been developed. In this study, we introduce a novel and, interpretable deep learning framework based on Graph Attention Networks (GAT) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to enable accurate diagnosis of SSc using serum anti-microbial IgM antibody data and uncover valid inter-bacterial relationships. We analyzed a dataset comprising 126 individuals (76 SSc and 50 healthy controls). To capture complex inter-species correlations often overlooked by conventional tabular data, we first converted the microbial profiles into a graph structure. The constructed ensemble model, combining GAT for relational feature extraction and CNN for hierarchical pattern recognition, achieved a high diagnostic accuracy of 0.9051, representing an improvement of up to 10.96 percentage points over recent comparable studies. To interpret the model's diagnostic rationale, we applied Association Rule Mining (ARM) to the latent representations from the proposed framework's intermediate layer. This analysis revealed significant clustering patterns, distinguishing groups with specific microbial combinations common in SSc patients, and these patterns that were rarely observed in healthy controls. Our work presents a novel methodology for interpreting deep learning predictions in healthcare and provides initial evidence for the diagnostic potential of this approach in a rare disease setting, using only a small set of core microbial combinations. These findings suggest the potential to enhance screening efficiency for SSc and provide hypothesis-generating insights into biological mechanisms underlying the disease, warranting further validation in larger, independent cohorts.

title: Prototype-driven contrastive learning enables transferable seismic representation
abstract: Deep learning has become increasingly important in seismic monitoring and analysis, yet most existing methods remain heavily dependent on large labeled datasets and often transfer poorly across tasks and regions. To address these limitations, this study proposes ConProSeis, a self-supervised pretraining framework for learning transferable representations from seismic waveforms. ConProSeis develops a prototype-driven contrastive strategy that uses diverse physics-guided multi-view augmentations to improve representation robustness and reduce semantic shifts caused by perturbations. Intra-prototype and inter-prototype contrastive losses are further introduced to enhance feature discrimination. A dual-encoder architecture is adopted, in which the target encoder is updated by exponential moving average to stabilize training. Experiments on a large-scale Chinese seismic dataset show that the learned representations transfer effectively to earthquake event classification, magnitude regression, and phase detection. In tectonic-versus-non-tectonic event classification, ConProSeis achieves an accuracy of 99.03%. Additional experiments on the Pacific Northwest dataset further demonstrate cross-regional transferability. Overall, the results suggest that physics-aware self-supervised pretraining can reduce label dependence and improve the robustness and transferability of seismic representation learning.

title: A hybrid transformer-based multi-task framework for rapid seismic response prediction of reinforced concrete chimneys
abstract: Reinforced concrete (RC) chimneys represent critical industrial infrastructure with significant seismic vulnerability due to their slender and high-rise geometry. Conventional nonlinear numerical simulations, while accurate, are computationally expensive and unsuitable for real-time response prediction and large-scale parametric investigations. This study addresses these limitations by proposing a Deep Learning (DL) framework for fast and accurate prediction of dynamic seismic responses. A dataset of over 40,000 high-fidelity Nonlinear Time History Analyses (NLTHAs) was generated using OpenSees, incorporating diverse geometric configurations, and material nonlinearities subjected to real Ground Motion Acceleration (GMA) records scaled across multiple intensities. A hybrid Transformer-based architecture is proposed, utilizing a multi-task learning configuration with a shared encoder backbone, a transfer learning strategy and an adaptive sequence compression module. This design allows the model to simultaneously predict dominant modal frequencies and full dynamic response time histories, while effectively managing long-range temporal dependencies. The model demonstrates exceptional predictive accuracy on unseen test data, achieving Pearson correlation coefficients (R) exceeding 0.99 for modal frequencies and 0.98 for dynamic response time histories. It demonstrates promising generalization capability for previously unseen geometries and seismic waveforms, maintaining high fidelity in capturing peak responses, and phase alignment. The architecture reduces computational cost from several minutes per simulation to milliseconds per prediction. This efficiency enables near-instantaneous predictions, providing a practical tool for performance-based design and potential future integration into real-time structural health monitoring of critical industrial infrastructure.

title: Machine learning–integrated spatial decision framework for sustainable offshore wind and marine spatial planning: A Black Sea case study
abstract: A newly developed integrated Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP), Entropy Weight Method (EWM), Machine Learning (ML), and Half-Quadratic Programming (HQ Programming) framework within a Geographic Information System (GIS) environment was designed for offshore wind farm (OWF) site selection. This hybrid methodology was applied to the Samsun–Ordu–Giresun continental shelf along the southern Black Sea to identify technically feasible, environmentally compatible, and policy-relevant offshore wind development zones. The scientific problem addressed in this work is the limited ability of conventional GIS–multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approaches to reconcile uncertain expert judgments, objective spatial variability, and data-driven criterion relevance within a single transparent weighting structure. FAHP represented expert judgments under uncertainty, while EWM provided objective entropy-based weights derived from geospatial variability. Five supervised ML algorithms—Decision Tree, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Ridge Classifier, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Support Vector Machines (SVM)—were implemented using Annual Energy Production (AEP) as the target variable to quantify the empirical importance of spatial criteria. HQ Programming merged FAHP, EWM, and ML-based weights into a unified balance between subjective and objective assessments. Wind resource parameters contributed ∼18% to total suitability, infrastructural factors 16%, oceanographic–geophysical conditions 28%, and environmental–navigational constraints 30%. GIS-based analysis identified the Atakum–Ünye–Gülyalı corridor as the most favorable development zone. The framework helps decision-makers prioritize offshore wind investment areas, reduce conflicts with navigation and protected zones, and support grid- and port-oriented marine spatial planning. This study provides a transferable basis for explainable, data-calibrated spatial decision-making in offshore renewable energy planning.
