title: Recursive Multifactor Regression: A machine learning algorithm for pressure vessel nozzle stress estimation through closed-form expressions
abstract: Pressure vessels require explicit strength-assessment rules, yet current standards still lack closed-form rules for some critical nozzle configurations, which forces repeated Finite Element (FE) analyses. This paper introduces Recursive Multifactor Regression (RMR), an interpretable Machine Learning approach within Artificial Intelligence, to derive compact analytical formulas from FE-generated data. Unlike unconstrained symbolic regression, RMR explores a mechanically informed library of transformed variables and recursively selects a closed-form law using both standard statistical indicators and an engineering-oriented error-risk criterion. The method is applied to the estimation of the Tresca equivalent stress in the ligament between neighbouring nozzles located in the knuckle region of dished ends of pressure equipment. The retained formula yields less than 1% of relative errors beyond ± 30 % on the test set, and these rare exceedances occur only at stress levels well below the material yield strength. Additional benchmarks with ElasticNet and a shallow multilayer perceptron show that the response is learnable, while also indicating that RMR offers a more favourable compromise between predictive quality, compactness, interpretability, and direct usability as a design rule. The resulting expression supports comparative pre-sizing and can serve as a high-performance complement to repeated FE recalculations within the calibrated domain.

title: Paraffin wax–sand nanoparticles based heat transport of nanofluid in E-Shaped structures: Physics-informed neural networks
abstract: The wax sand nanoparticle in water advances thermal transport where controlled heat transfer is critical. The inclusion of wax enables latent heat storage, while sand nanoparticles stabilize temperature gradients. This combination improves heat transport rates under varying operating conditions. This research examines the effects of E-shaped geometry and wax–sand nanoparticle in water on transport manifestations using an physics-informed neural network structure. The governing nanofluidics model is established with nonlinear partial differential equations. Limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno algorithm is employed to ensure precise and steady convergence. The results exhibit that the E-shaped geometry upgrades spatial limitation and thermal performance, while the addition of wax and sand nanoparticles improves heat transfer properties. This neural scheme captures complicated physical behavior without demanding large datasets. The given framework indicates a reliable and dependable tool for analysis of ambiguous exchange phenomena in geometries relevant to cutting edge energy systems.

title: Mitigating measurement-induced training instability in hybrid quantum neural networks for protein classification
abstract: Hybrid Quantum Neural Network (QNN) classifiers produce logits as expectation values of quantum measurement operators. For standard Pauli measurements, these outputs are intrinsically bounded to the interval [ − 1,1 ] . When such bounded logits are used directly with the cross-entropy loss applied to softmax-normalized logits for multi-class classification, the loss function operates in a regime of weak sensitivity to logit differences. As a consequence, parameter gradients are suppressed, leading to unstable optimization in variational quantum classifiers (VQCs). In this work, we identify this effect as measurement-induced logit contraction , an underexplored source of trainability degradation in hybrid QNN. To address this limitation, we introduce a learnable scaling parameter, termed Quantum Measurement Temperature (QMT) , which rescales quantum measurement outputs prior to the loss. Unlike post-hoc calibration, QMT acts during training and compensates for the physically imposed bounds on quantum measurement outputs . This rescaling increases gradient magnitude and variance, thereby improving loss sensitivity. The proposed mechanism is architecture-agnostic and does not modify the quantum ansatz, circuit depth, or measurement operators. Experiments on fluorescence microscopy images and a six-class fashion image classification benchmark demonstrate that QMT consistently enhances logit separation, strengthens gradients, stabilizes training across random initializations, and improves classification accuracy, relative to unscaled measurement readouts. These results demonstrate that QMT enables stable and reliable training of hybrid QNN for practical applications.

title: Wavelet-enhanced hybrid state space and convolutional network for coronary artery segmentation
abstract: Accurate coronary artery segmentation in coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) remains challenging due to variable global topology, curved and narrowed regions, and fine branches. Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are widely used for medical image segmentation, their local receptive fields limit the modeling of long-range coronary structures. To address this limitation, we propose a hybrid network architecture that integrates CNNs with Mamba, a state space model with efficient long-range dependency modeling capability, for coronary artery segmentation. Firstly, we propose an encoder module called the wavelet-integrated Mamba, which combines the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) with Mamba to replace the conventional CNN encoder block. The Mamba module captures global dependencies, while DWT extracts multi-scale frequency-domain features, including low-frequency structural information and high-frequency detail information. This integration enhances the model’s ability to balance global and local structural representations. Secondly, we design a dual-plane scanning strategy to better capture topology-aware coronary features. Additionally, we propose a geometric region fusion loss function that combines region-level supervision with a soft-skeleton-based geometric constraint, encouraging better structural continuity and reducing fragmented predictions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method provides a favorable balance among regional accuracy, structural consistency, and boundary localization. On the public Automated Segmentation of Coronary Arteries (ASOCA) dataset, our method achieves 84.62% Dice and 83.57% centerlineDice (clDice). In an additional pulmonary artery segmentation study, the proposed method achieves 83.48% Dice and 83.61% clDice, suggesting its potential applicability to other tree-like tubular structures.

title: Cross-modal Orthogonal Adaptive Contrastive Learning for robust chest radiology report generation
abstract: Automatic generation of chest radiology reports is pivotal for clinical decision-making, as it reduces radiologists’ diagnostic workload and mitigates the risk of missed findings. However, effective cross-modal semantic alignment remains challenging due to two key issues: (1) the inherent heterogeneity in feature representations between image and text modalities, and (2) the lack of semantic awareness in conventional negative sample selection strategies. The former introduces redundant and interfering signals that degrade alignment quality, while the latter misclassifies semantically similar samples as negatives, blurring decision boundaries and weakening discriminative power. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework, Cross-modal Orthogonal Adaptive Contrastive Learning (COACL), which enhances image–text semantic alignment and improves chest report generation through three core components: (1) a Modal Orthogonalization Module (MOM) that applies Schmidt orthogonalization to decouple image and text features into orthogonal subspaces. (2) a Gated Fusion Module (GFM) with dual-stream gated architecture to dynamically highlight salient semantic regions and enhance modality complementarity. (3) an Adaptive Contrastive Learning Module (ACLM) that employs a triplet comparison mechanism to adjust negative sample hardness based on semantic similarity and feature uniformity, progressively sharpening decision boundaries. Experiments on the benchmark IU-Xray and MIMIC-CXR datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple metrics, and ablation studies substantiate the necessity of each module.

title: Data-driven deep learning model for critical heat flux occurrence prediction based on bubble dynamics in pressurized water reactors
abstract: Prediction of critical heat flux (CHF) in thermal systems, such as heat pipes, heat exchangers, and pressurized water reactors (PWRs) is crucial for ensuring reactor safety and operational efficiency. Traditional CHF prediction methods often rely on empirical correlations with limited applicability, failing to capture the complex, multi-scale physics of boiling phenomena. This study addresses this challenge by introducing a novel deep learning (DL) framework that directly leverages detailed bubble dynamics extracted from high-fidelity computational multifluid dynamics (CMFD) simulations to predict the likelihood of CHF occurrence. This approach moves beyond simplified correlations by harnessing the extensive information contained within the simulated boiling process. The novelty of this work is the development of an artificial intelligence (AI)-based predictive algorithm that directly integrates advanced bubble flow and heat dynamics. It achieves this by combining a machine-learning parameterized equation of state (EoS) with a robust coupled control volume and finite element method (CVFEM) model and a compressive advection interface capturing scheme (CAICM), forming self-adaptive, high-order accurate methods for detailed and precise CMFD simulations. Simulations provide a comprehensive dataset of bubble dynamics, which are then analyzed using the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) algorithm to extract key features. A DL model, trained on these extracted features, predicts CHF occurrence. This data-driven approach offers a significant advancement over existing methods by directly learning the complex relationships between bubble dynamics and CHF, providing a more accurate and physically grounded prediction. This high-accuracy framework improves PWR safety analysis and boiling heat transfer prediction for efficient reactor design.

title: A hybrid object detection and convolutional neural network framework for high-accuracy plant disease detection
abstract: Smart agriculture requires robust, real-time, and highly accurate plant disease identification systems capable of performing reliably across diverse environmental conditions. This paper presents a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates the You Only Look Once version 5 object detection model with a Convolutional Neural Network classification head for precise plant disease identification. The proposed pipeline begins with data acquisition using the Plant Diseases Classification benchmark dataset, followed by advanced preprocessing through the Perona-Malik Anisotropic Diffusion algorithm for noise suppression and Elastic Distortion for data augmentation. Disease-affected regions are then precisely isolated using Watershed-based gradient segmentation, after which Speeded-Up Robust Features extraction guided by Hessian-matrix keypoint detection is applied. The pipeline concludes with end-to-end classification using the proposed hybrid deep learning framework across four crop health categories: Healthy, Rust, Powdery Mildew, and Slug damage. Rigorous experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed model consistently achieves 98.97% accuracy, 98.86% precision, 98.88% recall, and 98.87% F1-score, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines, including EfficientNetwork, standalone You Only Look Once version 5, Vision Transformers, and standard convolutional neural network architectures, by margins of up to 5.97 percentage points over comparable deep learning baselines. Near-perfect agreement between model predictions and ground-truth labels is further supported by a Cohen's Kappa coefficient of 0.9843. The system's two-stage localisation architecture delivers a computationally efficient and scalable solution well-suited for edge deployment within Internet of Things-enabled precision agriculture systems. This work contributes a reproducible, mathematically grounded methodology alongside a comprehensive ablation study, establishing the proposed hybrid deep learning framework as a strong benchmark for automated crop health monitoring.

title: Multimodal attention fusion: Integrating proteomics and body composition for longitudinal type 2 diabetes risk prediction
abstract: Longitudinal analysis of high-dimensional biomedical data offers a transformative window into the transition from health to metabolic disease. Despite advancements in predictive modeling, the integration of temporal proteomic shifts with clinical phenotypes for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) risk assessment remains underdeveloped, particularly within underrepresented Middle Eastern populations. We developed an interpretable, deep-learning pipeline utilizing tabular network (TabNet), an attention-based architecture designed for tabular data, to analyze a longitudinal cohort from the Qatar biobank (QBB). The framework integrates multimodal inputs, including proteomic signatures, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) body composition metrics, and electronic health records (EHR). Model transparency was ensured through built-in feature selection and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values. The performance of the TabNet model was rigorously benchmarked against gradient-boosting machines, support vector machines, and random forest. Our findings demonstrate that the TabNet significantly outperforms conventional machine learning benchmarks in capturing the non-linear trajectories of diabetes progression. The model identified a distinct cluster of proteomic markers and visceral adiposity metrics that serve as early indicators of T2DM. Age-and-gender-stratified analyses revealed significant demographic divergence in risk profiles; specifically, the predictive weight of inflammatory markers and visceral fat mass exhibited profound variance across age cohorts, suggesting the need for life-stage-specific screening protocols. This study establishes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework that bridges the gap between molecular discovery and clinical risk stratification. By uncovering the demographic-specific drivers of T2DM, our results provide a foundation for personalized preventative medicine and highlight the efficacy of attention-based deep learning in managing complex, longitudinal biobank data.

title: A robust two-stage framework for microgrid economic dispatch integrating transfer learning-based informer and linear variational diffusion: Quantification and impact analysis of demand response delays
abstract: The growing penetration of renewables and flexible demand-side resources makes microgrid economic dispatch heavily dependent on accurate forecasting, uncertainty modeling, and reliable demand response (DR) execution. However, practical DR actions often suffer from demand response delays (DRD) after dispatch signals, causing deviations between scheduled and actual load adjustments. To address this issue, this paper proposes a DRD-aware economic dispatch framework for microgrids by integrating time-series forecasting, generative scenario construction, and robust two-stage optimization. In the forecasting stage, a transfer learning-based Informer (TL-Informer) model is developed, in which a three-stage fine-tuning strategy is adopted to improve short-term load prediction accuracy under limited-data conditions. To characterize forecasting uncertainty, a two-stage linear variational diffusion generation framework (LV-DGF) is further proposed. In the first stage, a linear transformer-based variational autoencoder (LTVAE) is designed to achieve efficient long-sequence modeling and heterogeneous feature embedding. In the second stage, a score-based diffusion model is introduced to perform latent-space sampling and reconstruction, thereby enhancing both the physical consistency and statistical diversity of generated scenarios. Based on the predicted load and generated uncertainty scenarios, a DRD-aware robust two-stage optimization model is established to quantify the impact of delayed DR on operating costs and scheduling performance. Case studies demonstrate that DRD significantly affects microgrid dispatch decisions, and that neglecting such delays may lead to underestimated operating costs and reduced scheduling reliability. The results confirm the practical applicability of the proposed framework in supporting delay-aware microgrid scheduling and cost evaluation.

title: Lightweight stage-wise deep learning framework for joint brain tumour segmentation and classification from magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: Accurate brain tumour analysis from magnetic resonance imaging requires both image-level classification and pixel-level segmentation. However, many deep learning approaches either handle these tasks separately or combine them in tightly coupled frameworks that may cause interference between tumour localisation and diagnostic prediction. This study proposes the Attention Long Short-Term Memory Segmentation Boundary Network (ALSB-Net), a lightweight stage-wise artificial intelligence framework for joint brain tumour segmentation and binary tumour/no-tumour classification. The artificial intelligence (AI) contribution is a stage-wise architecture that first learns tumour regions and boundary information using a constructed transfer-learning encoder incorporating selected transferred convolutional feature-extraction layers, bidirectional long short-term memory contextual modelling, attention refinement, and boundary-aware supervision, and then performs classification using detached feature representations to reduce task interference. The engineering application is demonstrated through integration into a Picture Archiving and Communication System-oriented research prototype for image viewing, reporting, and similar-case review. The framework was evaluated using an image/slice-level dataset combining public lower-grade glioma magnetic resonance imaging data with anonymised clinical scans collected from Iraqi hospitals. The classification dataset contained 5020 images, and the segmentation subset contained 3933 image-mask pairs. ALSB-Net achieved 95.4% classification accuracy, a 94.3% F1-score, and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve of 0.988. For segmentation, it achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.9250, an intersection over union of 0.8120, and a 95th percentile Hausdorff distance of 2.85 mm. With 8.5233 million parameters, the framework provides efficient AI-assisted brain tumour analysis, while broader multi-centre validation remains necessary before routine clinical deployment.

title: A comparison study of computational fluid dynamics and physics-Informed neural network modelling approaches for protein elution in non-binding liquid chromatography
abstract: Resin-based Liquid Chromatography (LC) is crucial for pharmaceutical manufacturing, but optimizing its process by conventional Design of Experiment is resource intensive. Numerical modelling techniques like Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) offer virtual platform to analyse flow and solute concentration distribution within LC column. Present study develops an opensource CFD solver under non-binding condition, benchmarking it against two experimental cases under different flow rates (Reynolds number in range of 0.02 to 0.096). The simulation results are in very good agreement with experimental ones (average coefficient of determination (R^{2}) score of 0.990 ± 0.003 for experimental case 1 and 0.969 ± 0.039 for experimental case 2). Further, an advanced meshless approach, Physics Informed Neural Network (PINN) is explored as a potential solver for the application of LC. A simplified 1-dimensional governing equation under non-binding is used for PINN based solver, and the predicted results are tested against experiment and CFD simulated results. For the studied range, PINN predicted results are in very good agreement with the experimental ones (average R^{2} of 0.990 ± 0.005 for experimental case 1 and 0.963 ± 0.047 for experimental case 2) and also replicated the CFD simulated ones with the advantage of reduced computational time (an average of 2.5 min for PINN versus 28 h of CFD simulations). However, the PINN predictions deviated from CFD result under high flow rate and strong dispersions (superficial condition for protein separation). For the studied LC conditions, the developed PINN based solver showed a promising alternative of conventional numerical modelling techniques.

title: Remote sensing optical image matching through neighborhood-aware global propagation in graph neural networks
abstract: Mismatch removal is a critical post-processing step for improving the reliability of remote sensing optical image matching. Existing methods generally rely on local-consensus verification, global geometric estimation, or dense graph-based reasoning. However, local approaches have limited receptive fields, global models are often inadequate for complex non-rigid or nonlinear distortions, and dense graphs may cause high computational cost and noisy message propagation. To address these issues, we propose a supervised graph learning framework that formulates mismatch removal as a graph neural network-based node classification task. Each putative correspondence is treated as a graph node, and motion-aware local preservation features are encoded using Kendall rank correlation and the longest common subsequence, providing discriminative cues for outlier rejection. To enhance efficiency and robustness, vector-field-consistency-based edge pruning is introduced to construct a sparse graph, suppressing unreliable message passing while reducing computational overhead. Built upon graph sample-and-aggregate network, the proposed network propagates neighborhood information through sparse global connections, effectively integrating local feature distinctiveness with global spatial coherence. Experiments on in-domain and cross-domain datasets show that our method achieves comparable or superior performance to representative state-of-the-art local-consensus, optimization-based, and learning-based methods. In cross-dataset mismatch-removal evaluation, the proposed method improves the F-score by up to 2.74 percentage points over the strongest competing verification baseline.

title: Multi-robot coordination for effective anomaly handling in self-driving laboratories
abstract: This study addresses multi-robot collaborative anomaly handling challenges in self-driving scientific laboratories, where anomalies cause distorted results, equipment damage and safety risks. For Artificial Intelligence (AI) contributions, we design a hierarchical large language model (LLM)-driven intelligent task planning framework for dynamic action decomposition and adjustment, and propose an anomaly-triggered cross-behavior tree expansion algorithm with a spatiotemporal propagation suppression strategy to realize real-time anomaly localization and management. For engineering applications, we build a high-fidelity simulation engine for silicone preparation and a physical multi-robot experimental system, designing three representative anomaly tasks (spatial, temporal, hybrid) for validation. Experimental results show that at 50% anomaly probability, the framework achieves a 78.67% task success rate (74.45% higher than the baseline) and shortens the task duration by 150 s (1476.67\to 1326.67 s). Both simulated and real-world tests verify that the proposed AI methods effectively enhance the system’s fault tolerance and flexibility. This work provides a novel AI-driven engineering solution for the full automation transformation of scientific laboratories.

title: Adaptive sampling meta-learned Gaussian processes for global sensitivity analysis of seismic responses with partial structural updating
abstract: Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) of nonlinear seismic responses is essential for identifying the dominant uncertain parameters governing structural performance, yet its practical application remains computationally demanding because it requires repeated nonlinear time–history analyses over uncertain parameter spaces. This challenge becomes even more severe in partial structural updating problems, where conventional surrogate models are typically reconstructed from scratch for each updated configuration, resulting in poor sample efficiency and limited reuse of previously acquired information. To address this issue, this study proposes an adaptive-sampling meta-learning Gaussian process framework for global sensitivity analysis (ASMLGP–GSA). The proposed framework transfers prior knowledge from structurally related meta-tasks to initialize the surrogate model of new target tasks, and then progressively refines the target-task surrogate through a cross-validation–Voronoi-based adaptive sampling strategy. A subdomain-importance stopping criterion is further introduced to terminate enrichment in a practical and computationally efficient manner. The framework is validated using three benchmark examples: a nonlinear two-degree-of-freedom Bouc–Wen system, a two-story steel moment-resisting frame equipped with self-centering viscous dampers, and a realistic three-dimensional offshore wind turbine jacket structure. The results show that the proposed method achieves high predictive accuracy while reducing the number of additional high-fidelity simulations required for convergence by approximately 80%–90% relative to single-task baseline methods. The surrogate-based Sobol’ indices also agree well with direct Monte Carlo estimates and correctly identify the dominant uncertain parameters in both case studies. These results demonstrate that ASMLGP–GSA provides an accurate and sample-efficient computational framework for seismic uncertainty propagation and sensitivity analysis of partially updated nonlinear structural systems.

title: Inverse design of mixture proportions for steel fiber-reinforced recycled aggregate concrete using interpretable machine learning and multi-objective optimization
abstract: Steel Fiber-Reinforced Recycled Aggregate Concrete (SFR-RAC) represents a sustainable alternative to conventional concrete, yet its mechanical properties exhibit high variability due to the coupled effects of recycled aggregate variability, steel fiber characteristics, and mixture proportions. This study develops a machine learning based reverse design framework to accurately predict key mechanical properties (i.e., compressive strength and splitting tensile strength) and optimize mixture proportions for SFR-RAC. Using a comprehensive dataset comprising 465 compressive strength samples and 339 splitting tensile strength samples, four machine learning algorithms (i.e., Extreme Gradient Boosting (i.e., XGBoost), Random Forest (i.e., RF), Decision Tree (i.e., DT), and K-Nearest Neighbors (i.e., KNN)) were trained and hyperparameter-optimized via Bayesian optimization with 5-fold cross-validation. In the case of the ensemble models (i.e., RF and XGBoost), both models exhibited better predictive capabilities. The RF model obtained test-set coefficient of determination values of 0.897 for the compressive strength parameter and 0.866 for the splitting tensile strength parameter, respectively, using Bayesian optimization. On the other hand, the XGBoost model obtained test-set coefficient of determination values of 0.893 for the compressive strength parameter and 0.896 for the splitting tensile strength parameter. Model interpretability was enhanced through Shapley Additive Explanations analysis, identifying water-to-binder ratio and steel fiber volume fraction as the most influential features for compressive strength and splitting tensile strength, respectively. Multi-objective optimization using Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II successfully generated Pareto-optimal solutions, balancing compressive strength and cost under practical constraints. This inverse design approach further provided actionable mixture proportions tailored to target performance criteria.

title: A Large Language Model-enhanced Delay-and-Sum algorithm for damage imaging in carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites
abstract: Carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites are widely used in aerospace structures, where internal delamination may pose serious safety risks. Ultrasonic guided-wave based structural health monitoring (SHM) has been extensively investigated for damage imaging. However, existing methods often exhibit limited effectiveness in accurately reconstructing irregular delamination damage. To address this challenge, this study proposes a Large Language Model-enhanced Delay-and-Sum (LLM-DAS) algorithm for pixel-level delamination imaging by integrating large language model (LLM) based multimodal inference with physics-based guided-wave reconstruction. First, the proposed Ultrasonic Guided Wave Large Language Model (UGW-LLM) automatically extracts and fuses damage-relevant information from multimodal monitoring data, including path-level time-series signals and specimen-level textual prompts. By leveraging the contextual reasoning capability of pretrained LLMs, UGW-LLM generates path-dependent damage-specific signals for each actuator–sensor path. Subsequently, based on guided-wave scattering theory, an improved Delay-and-Sum (DAS) algorithm maps these generated signals into pixel-wise damage intensities using numerically simulated group-velocity curves. Finally, the proposed LLM-DAS framework produces accurate and physically interpretable damage images without requiring LLM fine-tuning or manual threshold adjustment. Validation on CFRP laminates with three layup configurations demonstrates that LLM-DAS achieves Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) scores above 0.8920 on seen layups and above 0.8452 on unseen layups, significantly outperforming widely used guided-wave imaging methods.

title: Wind power forecasting via coupled dual-stage decomposition, adaptive component clustering, and a complexity-signal-to-noise ratio integrated index with deep learning
abstract:
Wind power time series are characterized by strong randomness, volatility, and non-stationarity, which poses severe challenges to accurate wind power forecasting and the stable operation of power grids. From an artificial intelligence (AI) perspective, this paper proposes a hybrid ultra-short-term wind power forecasting framework with three key methodological innovations: A data-driven adaptive component clustering strategy based on sample entropy and silhouette coefficient to objectively group wind power components; a Complexity-Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) Integrated Index (CSI) to guide secondary decomposition by combining structural complexity and signal quality; and a component-wise forecasting strategy with tailored deep learning models, including Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit with Attention (BiGRU-Attention), and Temporal Convolutional Network-Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit with Attention (TCN-BiGRU-Attention). From an engineering application perspective, the proposed method is validated on real-world wind power datasets from Wallonia, Belgium. Experimental results show that the method significantly outperforms benchmark models in terms of Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and coefficient of determination (
𝑅
2
), effectively improving forecasting accuracy and providing reliable technical support for the safe grid integration and efficient utilization of wind energy.

title: Physics-informed data-driven method for intelligent disc cutter wear multi-source information monitoring
abstract: Disc cutters are critical components of tunnel boring machines (TBM), yet existing wear monitoring methods are often restricted by harsh operating environments and still suffer from algorithmic limitations such as weak physical interpretability, insufficient generalization under varying operating parameters, and limited robustness when relying on single-source signals. This study proposes a novel intelligent disc cutter equipped with integrated temperature and vibration sensors. By establishing a dynamic model of the disc cutter, an Engineering-Optimized Physics-Data Neural Network (EOPD-NN) is utilized to reconstruct actual cutter ring loads. Furthermore, a decision-level information fusion framework—incorporating vibration, load, and temperature signals—is developed to predict the cutter wear state. The proposed monitoring algorithm relies only on localized cutter data. Experimental validation on a full-scale rotary cutting platform demonstrates that 94.29% of the sequence samples reconstructed by the EOPD-NN achieve a coefficient of determination (R^{2}) greater than 0.95 under different parameter conditions. Moreover, the proposed fusion strategy achieves a wear state recognition accuracy of about 96.5%. It also demonstrates exceptional interpretability within the domain. Ultimately, this intelligent disc cutter system offers a practical and reliable solution for cutter wear monitoring.

title: Deep learning for distributed acoustic sensing-based microseismic candidate-window classification in enhanced geothermal systems: A comparative study of twelve architectures
abstract: Microseismic event discrimination in distributed acoustic sensing data is critical for monitoring enhanced geothermal system operations, yet classical detectors based on short-term to long-term energy ratios, in the simple validation-tuned form evaluated here, fail to discriminate genuine seismic arrivals from structured noise. This paper presents a comparative study of twelve artificial intelligence models based on deep learning, spanning five architecture families—convolutional neural networks, transformers, recurrent networks, state-space models, and graph neural networks—benchmarked against three classical baselines on 3974 manually labeled distributed acoustic sensing recordings from a field stimulation campaign. We contribute an open-source labeling tool for multichannel seismic data, and evaluate complete 1.2-second triggered candidate-window classification rather than end-to-end continuous-stream detection. A preliminary temporal-context ablation is reported but not treated as a repeated-seed conclusion. The squeeze-and-excitation residual network and the plain residual network are statistically comparable; the squeeze-and-excitation variant has the highest numerical F1-score (the harmonic mean of precision and recall), 98.50%, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 99.46%, while the plain residual network has slightly stronger balanced accuracy and noise recall under the exported reviewer metrics. A selective state-space model achieves 95.76% F1-score, providing a competitive baseline for this architecture family in this dataset. A graph neural network exploiting fiber spatial topology achieves 95.47% F1-score with only 94,290 parameters. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping provides qualitative evidence that the convolutional models focus on primary-wave moveout patterns. To stress-test external transfer, all twelve saved Stage 14 models are evaluated without fine-tuning on Utah Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy April 2024 data, a different acquisition. The external set contains 4073 candidate windows (2024 event windows and 2049 non-event windows). The native records have 1496 traces and 4800 samples at 4000 samples per second; the same preprocessing function was used for event and non-event windows: the first 361 traces were retained, the records were downsampled to 2400 samples at 2000 samples per second using anti-aliased polyphase resampling, and per-channel z-score (zero mean, unit variance) normalization was applied. The best external model is the convolutional neural network–gated recurrent unit hybrid with F1-score 0.9930, balanced accuracy 0.9931, and Matthews correlation coefficient 0.9863. We interpret this as zero-shot evidence of matched-pipeline external robustness, not as universal cross-site validation or deployment-ready generalization. A three-seed retraining of the top two residual convolutional models with full random-state control further confirms that the small numerical F1 advantage of SE-ResNet over ResNet is within initialization variance: the pooled inter-seed standard deviation ( σ ≈ 0.0036 F1) is approximately four times the inter-model mean difference (0.0009 F1), and paired t -tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests fail to reject the null of no difference on F1, balanced accuracy, and MCC.

title: Real-time multi-constraint control of autonomous flexible endoscope robots via finite-time neural optimization
abstract: Autonomous flexible endoscope robots have shown great potential in reducing surgeon fatigue and improving visual stability in minimally invasive surgery (MIS). However, existing methods still face challenges in simultaneously enforcing multiple motion constraints required for safe and reliable clinical operation. To address this issue, this paper proposes a quadratic programming (QP)-based adaptive neural control framework that integrates multiple clinical constraints, including remote center of motion (RCM), joint-drift suppression, physical joint limits, and energy efficiency, into a unified formulation. To achieve efficient real-time optimization, a finite-time-convergent adaptive neural network (FST-ANN) solver is developed. The proposed solver incorporates an adaptive-gain mechanism to balance convergence speed and steady-state error, and employs a tailored activation function to ensure finite-time convergence. In addition, an oriented bounding box (OBB)-based surgical instrument detection method is introduced. A new dataset, namely the OBB-based Surgical Instrument Detection dataset (OBBSID), is constructed to provide fine-grained orientation and size information for robust instrument localization under varying illumination and occlusion conditions. Compared with conventional horizontal bounding box (HBB) representations, the proposed approach improves detection accuracy and robustness in complex surgical environments. The performance of the proposed framework is validated through numerical analysis, simulations, and preclinical porcine cadaver experiments. Results demonstrate effective multi-constraint control, faster convergence compared to existing methods, and reliable real-time instrument detection for surgical applications.

title: Utilizing machine unlearning for faulty behavior patterns in human decision-making model: A sharded reinforcement learning approach
abstract: In this paper, enhance the computational models of human decision-making by proposing a novel sharded reinforcement learning framework based on the principle of machine unlearning. The work proposes a data sharding and selective machine unlearning approach to unlearn faulty behavior patterns. It overcomes the drawbacks of conventional reinforcement learning methods, in which the players tend to play the same deck over and over again, showing a lack of adaptability. These problems are frequently seen in tasks such as the Iowa gambling task. To handle this issue, the concept of machine unlearning is used. The proposed method detects repeated patterns of faulty behavior, such as repeated deck selections. Such patterns are corrected locally at the level of shards, while retaining the last stable expectancy state from the previous learning stage. The mean squared deviation was used to evaluate the model's performance. The results indicate that the unlearned model learns faster and has better performance in the early phases of learning. The framework supports behavioral adaptability by selectively excluding identified faulty shards while preserving previous valid learning. These findings show the potential of shard-based learning and selective unlearning in sequential decision-making.

title: Machine learning–driven forecasting and robustness analysis of hybrid wind–solar energy systems for urban street lighting applications
abstract: This study proposes a data-driven optimization and analytical framework based on artificial-intelligence techniques for a hybrid wind and solar energy system designed specifically for urban street-lighting applications in İzmir, Turkey. The system integrates a vertical axis wind turbine with a helical blade configuration and photovoltaic (PV) panels to exploit complementary renewable resources under urban coastal conditions. Long-term meteorological assessment indicates favorable hybrid potential in the study area, characterized by strong wind availability and sufficient solar irradiance. To support reliable short-term power estimation, ensemble-based machine learning (ML) techniques are employed to forecast short-term power generation, including Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest algorithms. Model performance is evaluated using standard regression metrics, with XGBoost demonstrating the most consistent generalization performance across both wind- and solar-driven outputs. To enhance interpretability and address the limited transparency often associated with data-driven models, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis is applied to quantify the relative influence of environmental variables. The results reveal that wind speed, solar irradiance, and ambient temperature are the dominant drivers of hybrid energy production. Beyond predictive accuracy, the analysis incorporates urban operating constraints, demonstrating that hybridization substantially mitigates output variability under realistic urban wind conditions. Statistical and distributional analyses show that the hybrid configuration reduces overall power-output variability by approximately thirty-eight percent compared with standalone photovoltaic operation, thereby improving supply continuity for public lighting services. The novelty of this work lies in combining physics-informed energy modeling with explainable ensemble-based forecasting, explicitly tailored to urban street lighting applications rather than generalized power systems. By emphasizing predictive reliability, interpretability, and urban microclimatic relevance, the proposed framework provides a practically oriented basis for decentralized renewable energy planning in similar urban environments.

title: A novel automated deep learning framework for simultaneous brain tumour segmentation and classification from magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: Accurate brain tumour segmentation from Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) remains a major clinical challenge due to tumour heterogeneity, irregular morphology, blurred boundaries, low-contrast regions, and very small lesions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel lightweight deep learning framework for simultaneous brain tumour segmentation and classification based on the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) segmentation architecture. The framework incorporates a pathology-aware lightweight backbone, a scale-reallocated segmentation hierarchy, and an additional extra-small segmentation head to improve the detection of small and irregular tumours. A multi-scale feature fusion strategy enhances segmentation accuracy while reducing model parameters by 80.5% and computational complexity by 57% compared with the baseline model. In addition, a novel adaptive training strategy, termed Best Adaptation Strategy (BAS), improves convergence stability, optimisation robustness, and model generalisation during training. Extensive experiments were conducted using a brain tumour segmentation dataset containing 801 magnetic resonance imaging scans, and the Figshare Brain Tumour (FBT) dataset containing 3064 multi-class tumour scans. The proposed framework achieved mean Average Precision (mAP) values of 97.7% and 99.4% at an Intersection over Union (IoU) threshold of 0.50, and 83.1% and 83.3% across thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95, respectively. These results outperform recent standard deep learning segmentation models, classical machine learning approaches, and other state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, deployment on a robotic platform demonstrates the practical feasibility and translational potential of the proposed framework for real-time diagnosis in limited-resource environments and artificial intelligence applications in healthcare.

title: Accurate prediction of chemo-mechanical coupled full-field responses of battery electrodes using a deep learning scheme
abstract: Elucidating chemo-mechanical degradation mechanisms and optimizing the design of lithium-ion battery electrodes require a deep understanding of the coupled chemo-mechanical behavior within real heterogeneous microstructures. However, traditional microstructure-based finite element (FE) simulations are computationally prohibitive for resolving such complex three-dimensional (3D) multiphysics fields. In this study, an end-to-end deep learning scheme is developed to directly predict the 3D coupled chemo-mechanical full-field responses of electrode microstructures from geometric information, without requiring any additional prior physical information. The microstructural geometries are generated using a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based stochastic reconstruction algorithm trained on scanning electron microscope (SEM) images of real electrodes. The prediction model is built on a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) comprising a hybrid CNN–Transformer generator and a multi-scale discriminator. This architecture enables the simultaneous prediction of 3D stress and lithium concentration fields. The proposed framework demonstrates high predictive accuracy, achieving average relative errors of approximately 4.4% for stress fields and 1.5% for concentration fields. Experimental validation further supports the predicted heterogeneous lithium concentration distributions. By reducing inference time to only tens of seconds while maintaining accuracy comparable to high-fidelity simulations, this work provides an efficient alternative for rapid multiphysics analysis and microstructure design of battery materials.

title: Reliable deep diffusion tensor estimation: Rethinking the power of data-driven optimization routine
abstract: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) holds significant importance in clinical diagnosis and neuroscience research. However, conventional model-based fitting methods often suffer from sensitivity to noise, leading to decreased accuracy in estimating DTI parameters. While traditional data-driven deep learning methods have shown potential in terms of accuracy and efficiency, their limited generalization to out-of-training-distribution data impedes their broader application due to the diverse scan protocols used across centers, scanners, and studies. This work aims to tackle these challenges and promote the use of DTI by introducing a data-driven optimization-based method termed DoDTI. DoDTI combines the weighted linear least squares fitting algorithm and regularization by denoising technique. The former fits DW images from diverse acquisition settings into diffusion tensor field, while the latter applies a deep learning-based denoiser to regularize the diffusion tensor field instead of the DW images, which is free from the limitation of fixed-channel assignment of the network. The optimization object is solved using the alternating direction method of multipliers and then unrolled to construct a deep neural network, leveraging a data-driven strategy to learn network parameters. Extensive validation experiments are conducted utilizing both internally simulated datasets and externally obtained in-vivo datasets. The results, encompassing both qualitative and quantitative analyses, showcase that the proposed method attains state-of-the-art performance in DTI parameter estimation. Notably, it demonstrates superior generalization, accuracy, and efficiency, rendering it highly reliable for widespread application in the field.

title: Surrogate activated leaky integrate and fire neurons for electricity theft detection
abstract: Electricity theft is a major source of non-technical losses and poses a significant operational challenge for distribution system operators. While advanced metering infrastructure offers large-scale electricity consumption (EC) data, existing deep learning methods remain computationally expensive, prone to overfitting, and sensitive to class imbalance and high-dimensional inputs. This work proposes SSNet, a computationally efficient spiking neural network for electricity theft detection (ETD). SSNet employs leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons with surrogate gradients to capture temporal patterns in discrete EC measurements while substantially reducing computational overhead compared with conventional deep neural networks. To mitigate class imbalance, the proximity weighted synthetic oversampling (ProWSyn) technique is integrated to generate informative minority-class samples. In addition, a set of discriminative time-series features is extracted using the TSFEL framework to address high-dimensionality and enhance the separability of theft and non-theft profiles. SSNet is evaluated against several deep learning baselines and demonstrates superior performance, achieving 96.64% accuracy, 99.34% area under the curve (AUC), and 93.28% Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). The results highlight the potential of spiking neural architectures as efficient and high-performance solutions for large-scale ETD.

title: Deep learning for anomaly detection in railway systems: A structured survey
abstract: Ensuring safe and reliable operation of modern railway systems increasingly relies on data-driven monitoring and intelligent fault detection solutions. In recent years, deep learning has emerged as an effective paradigm for anomaly detection in railway applications, driven by the growing availability of heterogeneous sensor data collected from rolling stock and infrastructure. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of deep learning-based anomaly detection approaches developed for railway systems. The surveyed methods are systematically analyzed and organized using a unified taxonomy that captures the location of anomaly occurrence, data representation and manifestation, sensing modality, and temporal characteristics. Existing approaches, spanning convolutional neural networks, recurrent and attention-based architectures, autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, and transformer-based models, are further structured into major learning paradigms, including classification-based, prediction-based, reconstruction-based, and hybrid strategies. Beyond algorithmic design, this survey discusses key data-centric challenges and reviews commonly adopted evaluation practices and performance metrics. Practical deployment aspects are also addressed, including edge–cloud architectures, computational constraints, and hardware-aware optimization strategies for embedded railway applications. Building on this analysis, the survey introduces a decision-oriented framework that links anomaly characteristics, data properties, and operational constraints to appropriate detection paradigms and deployment configurations. By jointly considering learning models, data characteristics, evaluation protocols, and deployment constraints, this work provides engineers and researchers with a structured and application-oriented reference for selecting and deploying deep learning solutions for railway anomaly detection, while highlighting open challenges and future research directions toward reliable and scalable intelligent monitoring systems.

title: A Physics-Informed Kolmogorov–Arnold Graph Attention Network for solid mechanics on arbitrary geometries
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a formidable paradigm for solving partial differential equations governing physical systems. Even so, their efficacy has been largely confined to regular geometries limiting their real-world engineering application in solid mechanics where components possess the complex shapes and realistic boundary conditions. To bridge this critical gap, we introduce the Physics-Informed Kolmogorov–Arnold Graph Attention Network (PI-GKAT), a novel physics-informed graph neural network framework designed for high-fidelity solid mechanics simulations on arbitrary geometries. Our architecture integrates Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) into a Graph Neural Network (GNN) backbone. This structural enhancement unlocks superior function approximation, enabling the simulation of complex nonlinear mechanics on arbitrary geometries. Meanwhile, a Graph Attention (GAT) mechanism is integrated into the message-passing process, allowing the network to selectively weight and learn the most relevant local physical and structural information. This unified architecture supports a broad spectrum of constitutive models, including linear elasticity and hyper-elasticity, while accommodating realistic material parameters through physics-constrained loss functions. Extensive validation on multiple test cases with complex geometries demonstrates the superior generalization performance and higher predictive accuracy of the proposed PI-GKAT framework across different geometric shapes and material types. We also evaluated our framework on regular geometry and compared its performance with existing representative methods. PI-GKAT provides a robust and efficient tool for solving a new class of complex engineering problems.

title: Surrogate-constrained deep learning for inverse design in simulation-driven engineering: Application to plasmonic color generation
abstract: Simulation-driven inverse design problems are pervasive in engineering domains where evaluating candidate solutions requires expensive numerical solvers. This work proposes a general artificial intelligence framework for accelerating inverse design in complex engineered systems by coupling a forward surrogate model with an autoencoder-based inverse neural network. The framework addresses the inherent one-to-many nature of inverse mappings through a distribution-aware data generation and filtering pipeline, combined with an information-theoretic evaluation metric based on entropy and Kullback–Leibler divergence. The methodology is validated using a challenging nanophotonic case study involving plasmonic color generation from nanostructured metallic surfaces. A forward deep neural network is trained to approximate the mapping from geometric parameters to chromaticity coordinates, while an inverse deep neural network estimates feasible geometric configurations from target colors using a pretrained encoder–decoder architecture. The models are trained using 49,532 synthetic samples generated through numerical simulations and evolutionary optimization. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves an overall pipeline normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE) of 11.63%, an overall pipeline distributional similarity of 84.31%, and a reduction in inference time of 99.27% compared with simulation-based design. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed artificial intelligence (AI) framework as a practical surrogate for real-time and large-scale inverse design in engineering applications. Limitations related to extrapolation and reliance on synthetic data are discussed, and directions toward physics-informed learning and uncertainty-aware design are outlined.

title: Physics-informed neural network based on spatio-temporal information multiscale perception and adaptive memory for oceanic multiphysical fields modeling
abstract: Accurate prediction of ocean multivariable fields such as sea surface temperature, salinity, seawater flow rate and wind stress is crucial for understanding ocean–atmosphere interactions and climate prediction. However, the existing methods often have problems such as low accuracy, lack of physical consistency and poor long-term stability. To solve these problems, Multi-Physical Spatial–Temporal Adaptive Memory Network was proposed. This model utilizes the Multi-dimensional Feature Perception Module to adaptively extract features and calibrate important feature responses, constructs ocean physical dynamics constraints based on the Multi-Physics Ocean Cell, and models multi-dimensional long-term dependencies by introducing the Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Memory Unit. Experiments based on Hybrid Coordinate Ocean Model data show that our model outperforms 14 advanced and physics-guided benchmark models within a 7-day prediction period, performing well in the prediction of seawater velocity and wind stress direction. Even in the 28-day long-term prediction, it maintained excellent performance. It has good universality and stability, and can provide technical support for ship safety, fishery resource management and renewable energy development.
