title: Combination of Fourier Neural Operators and Bayesian Neural Networks to identify anisotropic thermal properties of Callovo-Oxfordian claystone from field heating tests integrating surrogate uncertainty
abstract: Reliable characterization of the thermal properties of Callovo-Oxfordian claystone is critical for the long-term safety assessment of deep geological nuclear waste disposal. This work addresses the Bayesian Inference of key parameters, including transversely isotropic thermal conductivity characterized by the perpendicular conductivity, the anisotropy ratio, equivalent density, specific heat capacity using experimental data from two heating experiments TED and ALC1604. For this aim, the forward problem is first modeled with a three-dimensional COMSOL Multiphysics simulation, and synthesis data per experiment are generated to train surrogate models. We evaluate several machine learning surrogates, including classical regression, deep neural networks, Fourier Neural Operators, and Bayesian Neural Networks. Fourier Neural Operators provides accurate deterministic emulation and serves as the baseline surrogate for Bayesian Inference. To overcome the overconfidence inherent in plug-in approaches, we propose uncertainty-aware surrogates by leveraging the predictive distribution of Bayesian Neural Networks. Three strategies are investigated: (i) CES-style likelihood, marginalizing surrogate uncertainty directly in the likelihood formulation, (ii) E-lik, explicitly incorporates surrogate variance in the likelihood function and (iii) E-pos, propagating surrogate uncertainty at the posterior level via mixtures of posteriors. Bayesian inference is performed with Markov Chain Monte Carlo, and results demonstrate that integrating surrogate uncertainty broadens posterior credible intervals, improves calibration, and avoids overconfident estimates compared to deterministic surrogates. Our findings highlight the importance of explicitly accounting for surrogate uncertainty in Bayesian inversion of computationally demanding uncertainty-aware thermal modeling problems and provide a framework for robust parameter identification of host rock in nuclear waste repository safety assessment

title: Evolvable physics-informed digital twin for real-time modeling and adaptation
abstract: This paper proposes an evolvable physics-informed neural network (PINN) for experimental digital twins (EDTs) of industrial systems for real-time modeling and adaptation. The framework integrates three components: system identification with dynamic modeling PINN, stable prediction using temporal contrastive learning, and adaptive parameter learning based on residual adapters. Experiments on permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) demonstrate high data efficiency, improved robustness, and strong generalizability over conventional models, with up to 1.82\times improvement in goodness of fit ({R}^{2}) under extreme data constraints while maintaining mean squared errors (MSEs) at 1{0}^{-1}–1{0}^{-2} under parameter drift. The framework provides a foundation for evaluating system behavior and optimal strategies in dynamic industrial environments.

title: Physics-informed neural networks for rapid flow field reconstruction in fluidized bed drying
abstract: To address the challenges of real-time observation of gas-solid two-phase flow and the high computational cost/lack of real-time capability of traditional Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations in fluidized bed drying processes, this paper proposes a rapid flow field reconstruction method based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). This method integrates sparse observation data with governing flow equations to achieve simultaneous prediction of key physical quantities including gas-phase velocity, solid-phase velocity, pressure, and solid volume fraction. A systematic evaluation was conducted under various conditions: spatial sparsity (20%, 5%, 1%), temporal sparsity (50%, 20%, 10%), noise interference (1%–20%), and cross-temporal extrapolation. Results show that with a spatial sampling rate as low as 5%, PINNs can still accurately reconstruct typical fluidization features such as bubble motion, solid-phase stratification, and pressure gradients. Even under an extreme sparsity of 1%, the overall flow pattern remains correct. Under dual spatio-temporal sparsity, the model demonstrates good information compensation capability, generating continuous and plausible transient evolution. With noise levels up to 20%, reconstruction errors exhibit only minor fluctuations, indicating strong noise resistance. Cross-temporal extrapolation experiments reveal that error growth over unseen time periods is steady and controllable, without non-physical oscillations. This study validates the stability, physical consistency, and robustness of PINNs under complex industrial scenarios involving sparsity, noise, and extrapolation, providing a viable technical pathway for real-time flow field reconstruction and intelligent monitoring in fluidized bed drying processes.

title: Closed-loop generative inverse design of lattice structures via reinforcement learning
abstract: Lattice structures are widely used in advanced engineering because of their lightweight characteristics and tunable mechanical properties. However, precise generative inverse design remains challenging because of the discrete combinatorial design space and nonlinear physical responses. Existing generative approaches often operate open-loop and focus on reproducing statistical distributions, making compliance with prescribed engineering targets difficult. To address this limitation, a performance-feedback-guided generative inverse-design framework integrates reinforcement learning (RL) with a physics-constrained conditional variational autoencoder (PC-VAE). The PC-VAE provides a continuous latent representation of discrete lattice topologies, while a pretrained surrogate supplies immediate performance feedback. The inverse-design stage is formulated as a one-step goal-conditioned contextual decision problem, in which a task-specific proximal policy optimization (PPO) policy learns a distribution over complete latent vectors from surrogate-based rewards. Policy updates increase the likelihood of candidates satisfying prescribed mechanical conditions while retaining alternative topologies. The framework is evaluated in six scenarios involving point-target, interval-constrained, and simultaneous two-property matching. Compared with the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES), PPO achieves comparable target-hit rates and consistently higher candidate uniqueness and topological diversity. Finite-element (FE) analyses of 48 prespecified validation structures were completed successfully. Median absolute surrogate-to-FE discrepancies were 3.03% for energy absorption and 3.88% for peak stress, with 87.50% of discrepancies within 10% for each property. For a given target, the method generates multiple topologically distinct structures with comparable mechanical responses, capturing the one-to-many relationship between prescribed properties and lattice topology. This study provides a flexible framework for target-directed generation of topologically diverse lattice candidates.

title: Deep learning-driven multisource remote sensing image fusion: Advances, challenges, and future directions
abstract: Multisource remote sensing image fusion has become an important solution to a long-standing limitation in Earth observation: individual sensors rarely provide high spatial detail, rich spectral information, reliable structural sensitivity, and frequent temporal coverage at the same time. This review examines how deep learning and artificial intelligence are being used to integrate multispectral, hyperspectral, panchromatic, optical, and synthetic aperture radar imagery for more reliable interpretation of complex ground scenes. It provides a technical synthesis of convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, transformer architectures, diffusion models, and hybrid model driven approaches, with attention to their fusion mechanisms, reconstruction behavior, computational demand, and suitability for operational use. Applications include land cover mapping, precision agriculture, environmental monitoring, urban analysis, disaster assessment, and defense related interpretation. Rather than treating each fusion task separately, this review connects sensor heterogeneity, spatial and spectral resolution trade offs, radiometric correction, geometric correction, registration, noise reduction, and fusion level design within a single framework. The analysis indicates that convolutional models remain effective for stable local detail recovery, adversarial learning can improve visual sharpness but may introduce spectral distortion, transformer models better capture long range spatial and spectral relationships, and diffusion models offer refined reconstruction at greater computational cost. The review further identifies open challenges involving misregistration, spectral bias, limited labeled data, weak generalization across sensors, high memory requirements, and limited interpretability. Future progress should prioritize sensor aware learning, self supervised training, uncertainty aware evaluation, lightweight deployment, and application oriented benchmarks to improve reliability in operational Earth observation.

title: From narrative to action: A hierarchical cognitive large language model agent framework for interpretable and adaptive human mobility behavior generation
abstract: Understanding and replicating human mobility requires not only spatial–temporal accuracy but also an awareness of the cognitive hierarchy underlying real-world travel decisions. Existing approaches often lack interpretability and struggle to represent adaptive behavior under changing constraints. This study proposes a Narrative-to-Action hierarchical large language model agent framework that models human mobility as a cognitively interpretable, multi-level process. The framework decomposes mobility generation into macro-level narrative reasoning, meso-level reflective planning, and micro-level behavioral execution, enabling agents to produce semantically coherent and structurally executable daily schedules while allowing dynamic adjustment in response to contextual changes. A key component is a reflective mechanism drawing on Mobility Entropy by Occupation, which captures heterogeneous behavioral flexibility across occupational groups. Empirical evaluation using travel diary data from Guangzhou demonstrates improved fidelity across spatial, temporal, and semantic dimensions compared to baseline approaches. Overall, by explicitly modeling how individuals reason about and adapt to constraints, the framework provides a behaviorally grounded and interpretable approach for mobility analysis, providing a basis for more transparent future evaluation of policy interventions and equity impacts.

title: Explainable artificial intelligence for deep learning-based delamination detection in Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer composites
abstract: The heterogeneous and anisotropic nature of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers (CFRP) introduces challenges in characterizing failure mechanisms, particularly delamination, in advanced composite engineering structures used across multiple industrial sectors. Although deep learning models, especially Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have demonstrated high diagnostic performance in Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), their inherent black-box nature limits interpretability and trust, thereby restricting deployment in real-world engineering applications. To address these limitations, this work proposes a methodology that integrates deep learning with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to enable transparent and reliable delamination detection in CFRP structures. The main contribution in Artificial Intelligence lies in the integration of convolutional neural networks with time–frequency representations of guided-wave signals and model-agnostic explainability techniques for intelligent fault detection in composite materials. From an engineering perspective, the proposed approach is applied to SHM and delamination diagnosis of CFRP specimens subjected to fatigue loading in engineering systems using Lamb waves acquired by piezoelectric transducers. The recorded Lamb wave signals were transformed into time–frequency representations and used as inputs to multiple CNN architectures, evaluated under a leakage-controlled, leave-one-cycle-out cross-validation protocol with multi-seed statistical aggregation, achieving accuracy values of up to 95.9% with statistically validated inter-architecture comparisons The explainability analysis highlighted physically meaningful indicators of delamination, such as amplitude attenuation and frequency shifts, demonstrating the potential of the proposed framework as an intelligent decision-support tool for fault detection and monitoring in engineering applications involving composite structures.

title: A Large Language Model-based Generative Artificial Intelligence and hybrid machine learning framework for prediction and inverse design of jute fiber concrete
abstract: The construction industry requires sustainable alternatives to conventional concrete to reduce environmental impacts while maintaining structural performance. Jute fiber concrete (JFC) is a promising low-carbon material; however, optimizing its mechanical properties is challenging because of complex nonlinear interactions among fiber characteristics and mix-design parameters. This study proposes an integrated framework combining Generative Artificial Intelligence (GEN-AI) with Decision Tree Boosting (DT-Boosting), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and GPR enhanced with Bayesian Optimization (GPR-BO) to predict and optimize JFC mechanical properties. An experimental dataset containing six input variables were expanded using a Large Language Model-based GEN-AI approach and validated through distribution analysis, boxplot comparisons, and Kendall correlation analysis. GPR-based models significantly outperformed DT-Boosting, reducing prediction errors by approximately 40–50%. The GPR-BO achieved the most consistent performance, with testing R^{2} values of 0.9242 for compressive strength and 0.9682 for tensile strength. However, the SHAP and Partial Dependence Plot analyses identified jute fiber volume fraction and fiber content as the most influential parameters, while the water–cement ratio exhibited a strong negative effect. Probabilistic validation confirmed accurate reproduction of strength distributions. Furthermore, integrating GPR-BO with NSGA-II enabled inverse mix design, automatically generating optimized JFC mixtures satisfying user-defined mechanical performance requirements. The optimization employed six mix-design decision variables and minimized both normalized prediction error and fiber volume fraction to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. The resulting framework extends forward prediction to practical inverse design, reducing trial-and-error experimentation and material waste while supporting resource-efficient, performance-based, and sustainable concrete mix development for engineering applications.

title: Physics-informed data-driven framework for predicting hall-controlled nanofluid transport in thermal engineering systems
abstract:
The present study introduces a physics-based data-driven surrogate modeling scheme with the intention of increasing the predictive potential of Hall-current driven nanofluidic transport in magnetically controlled thermosystems. Although numerous numerical simulations have been conducted on such a system, there is a dearth of AI based predictive tools for engineering design. The authors perform high fidelity numerical simulations by accounting for effects of nonlinearity of the thermal radiation, Brownian motion of the nanoparticles and thermophoresis in order to generate a validated engineering dataset for comparing Hall and non-Hall operating regimes. Results of the study demonstrate that Hall current greatly affects the boundary layer flow by causing transverse cross flow and altering momentum distribution, which leads to significant changes in the surface shear. Increase in the value of the Hall parameter causes suppression of thermal and solutal transport as seen from decreased values of the Nusselt number and the Sherwood number, especially in cases of strong magnetic interactions. In the current research, suction is identified as the main factor contributing to drag and heat transfer, while heat generation and nanoparticle diffusion reduce thermal performance. title: A secure federated learning framework with blockchain-based authentication for anomaly detection in cooperative smart farming
abstract: Agriculture is still a crucial global pillar of the world economy, ensuring food security and livelihood. But changing climate conditions and increasing reliance on the Internet of Things (IoT) based precision agriculture have brought new challenges, mainly cybersecurity. Cooperative Smart Farming (CSF) schemes promote resource pooling among small farmers and thus, the adoption of cutting-edge technologies. Although democratizing precision farming also makes it more accessible to cyber threats. To sort out all these problems, the proposed method introduces a secure federated learning framework along with blockchain-based authentication for anomaly detection in CSFs. The proposed method employs a federated transfer learning-based shadow attention mechanism, in conjunction with the Zeiler and Fergus network, to amplify the performance of the anomaly detection technique. This allows farms to detect threats in premises while protecting data privacy, as only model updates that are encrypted are transmitted. A blockchain-backed decentralized authentication scheme based on the proof of authentication consensus protocol is built to provide trust and resistance to tampering. Moreover, the random k-sparsification technique with changing rank adjustment has a positive impact on communication efficiency, which results in the same level of accuracy but with less communication overhead. The proposed method is executed on four datasets, CSE-CIS-IDS2018, MQTTset, ToN-IoT, and Edge IoT, achieving classification accuracies of 99.99%,99.93%,99.94%, and 99.91%, respectively, and it performs better than the current techniques. This comprehensive framework provides a scalable and trusted method for anomaly detection in CSFs, enabling resilient, privacy-preserving, and intelligent smart farming ecosystems.

title: Pipe flow of thixotropic fluids: Experiments, simulations and neural networks
abstract: Thixotropy refers to the time dependent evolution of a material’s microstructure, where structural agglomerates are progressively broken down under shear and rebuild when flow ceases. This study examines how such microstructural dynamics influence the transient pressure response of thixotropic yield stress fluids in laminar pipe flow. Experiments on Laponite suspensions performed with a custom built pipe rig reveal a pronounced decay in pressure drop over time at constant flowrate, reflecting shear induced structural breakdown. Complementary computational fluid dynamics simulations based on the Houska thixotropic constitutive model reproduce the experimental observations and elucidate the interplay between structural breakdown and recovery that governs the evolution of flow. The simulations capture the transition from plug-like to shear thinning dominated velocity profiles as flow rate increases, accompanied by a reduction of unyielded regions. To reduce computational cost, a feed-forward neural network surrogate trained on a limited set of experimental and simulated data accurately predicts the time-dependent pressure drop across a wide range of flow conditions. The integrated experimental, computational, and data driven framework establishes a quantitative basis for modeling and predicting the unsteady transport behavior of thixotropic fluids in pipe flow.

title: Artificial Intelligence-enhanced fine-grained anomaly detection for human-robot collaborative assembly
abstract: Human-robot collaborative assembly (HRCA) extends traditional manual assembly by synergizing human cognitive flexibility with robotic precision, and has become an important manufacturing paradigm in Industry 5.0. However, this synergy is frequently compromised by subtle human errors, whose automated detection presents a formidable challenge. This difficulty is fundamentally rooted in the visual ambiguity arising from high similarity in color, texture, and geometry between components and their assembly substrates. These conditions create low-contrast scenarios that obscure the fine-grained anomaly detection, such as minor positional offsets, rotational skews, and incorrect part substitutions. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-driven vision framework for fine-grained anomaly detection, enabling reliable in-process quality control for HRCA. The framework integrates three synergistic modules in a cohesive pipeline involving state perception, recognition and localization, and state discrimination. Firstly, a multi-task Keypoint Transformer U-Net (KP-TransUNet) performs concurrent component segmentation and keypoint detection with sub-pixel accuracy, establishing a robust foundation for geometric registration even in visually challenging environments. Subsequently, an improved You Only Look Once version 11 (Improved-YOLO11) algorithm precisely identifies and localizes assembly components. Finally, an Intersection over Union (IoU)-mask matching strategy combines box-level semantic matching with mask-level geometric deviation analysis to quantitatively discriminate among six typical assembly states. The efficacy of the proposed framework was empirically validated through a comprehensive case study on a satellite box assembly, achieving an overall anomaly detection accuracy of 97.30%.

title: Recursive online learning for stable long-term prediction of turbulent flows
abstract: Accurate long-term prediction of turbulent flows remains a key challenge in data-driven modeling owing to compounding errors during recursive rollout. We propose a recursive online learning (ROL) algorithm that incorporates simulation feedback into the learning process so as to reduce local prediction errors on surrogate-generated states encountered during long-horizon recursive rollout. We validated the ROL algorithm on both statistically stationary and extremely transient turbulent channel flows using several deep learning architectures. The results show that ROL consistently improves long-term stability and accuracy across the tested network architectures, even in a bypass-like transition. Importantly, ROL-enhanced models generalize robustly to strong noise perturbations and to larger domains beyond the training size while maintaining physically consistent turbulence dynamics. In addition, the trained models achieved speed-ups ranging from 33 × to 231 × relative to a graphics processing unit (GPU)-parallelized numerical solver. The proposed method is effective across the diverse network architectures tested, and enables fast and accurate inference, making it useful in scientific simulations that require robust long-horizon predictions.

title: Three-dimensional cementing displacement efficiency prediction based on domain-decomposed physics-informed neural network
abstract: Efficient displacement of drilling fluid by cement slurry is essential for ensuring cementing quality, and accurate flow-field prediction is crucial for improving displacement efficiency. Although computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is widely used to investigate displacement mechanisms, high-fidelity three-dimensional simulations are computationally expensive and inefficient for rapid engineering prediction and optimization. In recent years, data-driven neural networks have attracted attention due to their high computational efficiency; however, they rely heavily on large datasets, are prone to overfitting, and may produce predictions that violate physical laws. To address these issues, this study incorporates the governing fluid dynamics equations into the loss function of a deep neural network to impose physical constraints on flow-field evolution. Furthermore, a domain-decomposed physics-informed neural network (DD-PINN) is developed by dividing the computational domain into multiple coupled subdomains. Through parallel training and collaborative solving, the method alleviates convergence difficulties and instability commonly encountered by conventional PINNs in complex three-dimensional flow problems. Numerical experiments based on multi-condition three-dimensional datasets show that DD-PINN achieves higher prediction accuracy for pressure, velocity, and cement slurry concentration fields compared with purely data-driven models. For example, in predicting cement slurry volume fraction, the mean absolute error (MAE) is reduced from 1.27×10⁻² to 2.35×10⁻³. Compared with conventional PINN, the proposed method also significantly improves computational efficiency while maintaining comparable accuracy. Additionally, it enables quantitative evaluation of displacement efficiency and provides guidance for parameter optimization in cementing operations.

title: Seismic fragility prediction models for masonry buildings considering integration algorithms and deep learning frameworks
abstract: The seismic fragility of masonry buildings have been ubiquitously discussed in multiple zones worldwide. However, field inspection and data collection after earthquakes demonstrate the disadvantages of being time-consuming and labour-intensive, which poses a challenge for quickly obtaining the seismic fragility features of masonry structure clusters. To improve the efficiency of earthquake damage prediction and the rapid estimation of the seismic fragility of masonry structures, a seismic fragility prediction model for masonry buildings involving gradient boosting machine (GBM), categorical boosting (CatBoost), and feedforward neural network (FNN) methods was developed via intelligent ensemble algorithms and deep learning techniques. Using dynamic response analysis and earthquake risk assessment processes, dynamic responsiveness, hazard analysis, and intelligent model development were conducted on 2,598,972 accelerations monitored by the Wenchuan earthquake (May 12, 2008) array group in China. A dataset of 2211 masonry buildings (investigated by the author) in Dujiangyan city was thoroughly analysed, and a fragility matrix considering the optimised seismic vulnerability (damage) grade was proposed. The input variables of the learning model were the construction year, major story, foundation, function, and instrument intensity; moreover, a sensitivity analysis of the characteristic parameters was conducted. The optimised vulnerability (damage) grade of masonry structures was used as the output variable of the integrated and deep learning models. Using the established database, 20% and 80% of the structural damage instances were stratified and selected for testing and training model development, respectively. An analytical (precision-recall) curve was generated to evaluate the correlation between the predicted parameters of a learning model. To confirm the predictive precision of the developed learning model, a set of seismic fragility comparison curves for masonry buildings considering intelligent and empirical data-driven strategies was generated.

title: Deep reinforcement learning for autonomous driving decision-making: Algorithms, applications and challenges
abstract: Autonomous driving has the potential to greatly enhance road safety, traffic efficiency, and overall transportation effectiveness. The decision-making module serves as the core intelligence of the system, producing high-level commands for lane keeping, lane changing, and adaptive cruise control. Deep reinforcement learning has emerged as a pivotal approach in this domain, owing to its capacity to learn driving strategies through environmental interaction. This paper presents a systematic review of decision-making methods based on deep reinforcement learning for autonomous vehicles. It starts by outlining the general architecture of autonomous driving systems and emphasizing the central role of the decision-making module. The paper then explains the theoretical foundations of deep reinforcement learning, along with their applicability in driving decision tasks. Through a range of common driving scenarios, including lane keeping, lane changing, overtaking, and intersection navigation, the paper analyzes the decision-making advantages of deep reinforcement learning in complex and dynamic settings. Furthermore, it addresses key challenges in applying deep reinforcement learning to driving tasks. Compared to existing reviews, this study provides a systematic analysis of deep reinforcement learning in multiple decision-making scenarios for autonomous driving, overcoming the limitation of previous reviews that often focus on single scenarios. Adopting a progressive narrative structure, from single lateral or longitudinal control to increasingly complex tasks involving lateral-longitudinal coordination, it systematically clarifies the characteristics of different deep reinforcement learning algorithms and their applicable conditions. This structured approach helps researchers select appropriate algorithms and fusion strategies when facing driving scenarios of varying complexity.

title: Separated-variable spectral neural networks with characteristic-frequency multi-level initialization for high-frequency partial differential equations
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have emerged as a mesh-free paradigm for solving Partial Differential Equations (PDEs), yet a spectral bias severely limits their ability to resolve high-frequency components of oscillatory problems, and conventional Fourier-feature remedies scale exponentially with dimension. To overcome these limitations, we propose Separated-Variable Spectral Neural Networks (SV-SNN), a physics-informed framework with three core innovations. First, a separated-variable spectral representation expresses multivariate solutions as sums of $N$ separable modes, each a product of univariate adaptive Fourier spectral factors with $K$ frequencies per direction; this unites the dimensional scalability of variable separation with the frequency control of spectral methods, reducing the number of trainable parameters from order ${K}^{d}$ of tensor-product spectral bases to order $dNK$, linear in the dimension $d$, while admitting closed-form spatial derivatives through a hybrid differentiation strategy. Second, a characteristic-frequency multi-level sampling strategy allocates spectral resources across low-, characteristic-, and high-frequency bands, thereby targeting spectral bias and reducing sensitivity to frequency-estimation errors, with the characteristic frequency estimated automatically when not available a priori. Third, an effective-rank diagnostic derived from the singular value decomposition of the residual Jacobian quantifies spectral-bias severity a posteriori, explaining why standard architectures fail on oscillatory problems and guiding architecture selection. Across nine benchmarks—high-wavenumber heat and Helmholtz equations, nonlinear elliptic and Poisson problems on complex domains, and incompressible Navier–Stokes flows—SV-SNN achieves lower error than every competing baseline in matched-budget comparisons, by factors of 1.9 to 94, and remains more accurate even when baselines are afforded 15 to 200 times more parameters. Training completes within 11 to 34 s per problem on a single graphics processing unit. SV-SNN thus provides an accurate and parameter-efficient framework for wave propagation, heat conduction, and incompressible flow simulation. The source code is available at https://github.com/xgxgnpu/Physics-informed-vibe-coding/tree/main/SV-SNN.

title: A cross-scale meteorological-prior-informed adaptive fusion framework for ultra-short-term wind power forecasting
abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind power in electricity grids, accurate wind power forecasting (WPF) has become crucial for maintaining grid stability. Existing data-driven methods, while proficient in nonlinear modeling, are fundamentally limited by a lack of explicit cross-scale meteorological context. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces Global-Regional Cross-scale Meteorological Integration for Wind Power Forecasting (GRCMI-WPF), a cross-scale meteorological-prior-informed adaptive fusion framework that incorporates artificial-intelligence-weather-model-derived atmospheric context from global weather models into local ultra-short-term WPF. Through a dedicated Global-Regional Cross-scale Meteorological Integration (GRCMI) strategy, the framework extracts and injects multi-scale meteorological context surrounding target wind farms as weather-forecast-derived meteorological priors into the forecasting pipeline. Within this framework, we further propose the Dynamic Context-dependent Fusion Network (DCFNet), which employs a Hierarchical Cross-modal Alignment Transformer (HCAT) to effectively mitigate the dimensional and semantic disparities between heterogeneous meteorological priors and power series, and a Dynamic Context-dependent Fusion Gate (DCF-Gate) to adaptively allocate soft weights between historical power and meteorological modalities, achieving context-aware meteorological-prior-informed fusion. Extensive experiments on five real-world wind farm datasets demonstrate that the proposed GRCMI-WPF consistently outperforms the considered contemporary baselines under a unified evaluation protocol, confirming the value of integrating cross-scale meteorological priors for improving local WPF accuracy.

title: Embedded artificial intelligence in battery management systems: Pruning and quantization for efficient state-of-charge and state-of-health estimation
abstract: Online battery management requires accurate state-of-charge (SOC) and state-of-health (SOH) estimates within strict memory and timing budgets. To address these constraints, this work investigates how stateful long short-term memory (LSTM) networks with multi-layer perceptron (MLP) heads can be optimized for embedded artificial intelligence (AI), using structured pruning and recurrent-weight quantization to reduce memory and computational costs while retaining estimation accuracy on an STM32H753ZI microcontroller. Using the open Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) Cycle Ageing Dataset, full-precision models provide the accuracy reference against which the compressed variants are evaluated. Long-horizon replay yields mean absolute error (MAE) values of 2.3–2.8 percentage points for SOC and 0.9–1.5 for SOH, showing that compression largely preserves accuracy. The evaluated 30% pruning configuration reduces flash by 37.2% and 43.3% in the available firmware builds and inference time by 42.9% and 44.0% in the recorded hardware-in-the-loop benchmarks for SOC and SOH, respectively. The analytical complexity model relates computational savings to pruning fraction and network dimensions. Quantization reduces flash by 49.7% and 55.9% relative to the respective full-precision models, but raises runtime in the mixed-precision implementation. Together, the study provides a reproducible reference for resource-efficient embedded battery-state estimation.

title: Automated measurement of rural highway widths using transformer-based models and point cloud analysis
abstract: This study presents an automated method for extracting roadway width measurements and lane counts from Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR)-derived point clouds of rural highways and evaluates the reliability of measurements obtained from point clouds labeled by a Transformer-based point classification model. The proposed approach was evaluated on five highway segments in Alberta, Canada, encompassing both multilane and two-lane, two-way (TLTW) highways. From an artificial intelligence perspective, the study proposes a hierarchical Transformer-based semantic segmentation strategy with a geometry-aware measurement algorithm to estimate traveled way widths, shoulder widths, and lane counts directly from three-dimensional point cloud data. Automated measurements derived from manually labeled point clouds demonstrated strong agreement with manual reference measurements, with correlation coefficients exceeding 0.99 and mean absolute errors on the order of only a few centimeters for traveled way and shoulder widths. When applied to point clouds automatically segmented by the Transformer-based models, the framework continued to produce reliable results, with width estimation errors generally remaining within sub-meter ranges. Paired statistical tests indicated no statistically significant differences between automated and reference measurements at the 95% confidence level. Multiple lane count estimation strategies were evaluated, with lane-surface-based methods demonstrating increased robustness in scenarios where pavement markings were partially occluded or inconsistently detected. The results confirm that Transformer-based semantic segmentation, when combined with geometry-aware post-processing, can support accurate and scalable roadway geometry extraction from mobile LiDAR data. The proposed framework reduces reliance on manual surveys and offers a practical solution for automated roadway inventory generation and data-driven infrastructure management.

title: A component-aware progressive transfer learning method for wind power forecasting in newly built wind farms
abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting is essential for wind farm operation and grid integration. However, newly built wind farms often have limited historical data, restricting the performance of data-driven models. Under data scarcity, conventional deep learning models tend to overfit, while direct transfer learning may introduce irrelevant source-domain information when source and target farms differ. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a component-aware progressive transfer learning method for newly built wind farms. Relevant source wind farms are first selected based on combined power-sequence and meteorological similarity to reduce negative transfer. The original power sequence is then decomposed into trend and fluctuation components, which are modeled using a multilayer perceptron and a conditional generative adversarial network, respectively, and integrated through attention-based fusion. Rather than fine-tuning the entire model simultaneously, the proposed strategy progressively adapts the trend predictor, fluctuation model, and fusion module. Experiments on three newly built wind farm datasets yielded root mean square errors of 0.8850, 2.5060, and 5.0429 MW, representing reductions of 35.29%, 25.71%, and 33.03% over the best-performing benchmarks. On a United States dataset, the method achieved a root mean square error of 0.6543 MW and a coefficient of determination of 0.9870 for 15-min-ahead forecasting, while retaining its advantage over the comparison methods for forecasts 30 and 60 min ahead. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of source relevance selection, component-specific modeling, and progressive transfer learning under limited target-domain data.

title: Uncertainty-aware prediction of asphalt pavement roughness using probabilistic machine learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of asphalt pavement deterioration is critical for data-driven infrastructure asset management. However, conventional data-driven models commonly provide deterministic estimates, offering limited insight into prediction confidence. This limitation restricts their application in risk-aware decision-making, where understanding the reliability of each prediction is essential. This study addresses this challenge by developing an uncertainty-aware framework for predicting pavement roughness using data from the Long-Term Pavement Performance program. A curated dataset of 1,246 test sections across 50 states in the United States was compiled, covering diverse climate regions, structural configurations, traffic loading, and surface characteristics. Probabilistic modeling approaches, including Bayesian neural networks and Gaussian process regression, were used to predict pavement roughness while generating prediction intervals. Deterministic approaches, including random forest, extreme gradient boosting, support vector regression, and artificial neural networks, were also developed under the same validation and optimization framework for benchmarking. All models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation and optimized using a Bayesian optimization framework. The results showed that extreme gradient boosting achieved the highest point prediction accuracy, while Gaussian process regression and Bayesian neural networks provided competitive accuracy, with coefficients of determination of 0.9133 and 0.9226, respectively, along with explicit uncertainty estimates. Gaussian process regression also demonstrated a reliable uncertainty calibration, with empirical coverage of 95% prediction intervals ranging from 88.89% to 96.31% across climate regions. Initial roughness, rutting, and cracking were identified as the dominant predictors. Regional analyses further revealed generally lower prediction errors in non-freezing regions, and spatial analyses identified geographic variations in pavement deterioration.

title: Safety evaluation of new energy three-electric systems using enhanced physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Accurate safety-state measurement of the three-electric system in new energy vehicles is essential for ensuring reliable and secure operation. This paper proposes an artificial-intelligence-assisted safety measurement framework that integrates a searchable encryption mechanism with Enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks (EPINNs). In the proposed framework, the searchable encryption module supports privacy-preserving storage and retrieval of multi-source measurement data, while EPINNs serve as the core Artificial Intelligence (AI) model for multi-parameter state estimation and fault identification. A lightweight searchable encryption scheme based on block mapping is first designed to achieve feature-level obfuscation and protect sensitive measurement data. Then, an EPINNs-based state estimation model is developed by incorporating data-driven learning, subsystem physical constraints, and energy-consistency terms to enhance robustness under noisy sensor data. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves improved performance compared with conventional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models in battery state-of-health estimation, motor fault detection under injected fault conditions, and microgrid load measurement, with the motor fault detection accuracy exceeding 95% under the tested conditions. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an effective and secure technical solution for intelligent safety monitoring of new energy vehicle three-electric systems.

title: Physics-guided interpretable machine learning for explicit resistance equation discovery in concrete penetration
abstract: Classical Forrestal penetration calculations are attractive because they are explicit, but their empirical strength-only resistance term is too restrictive for heterogeneous concrete-penetration data. This study derives a closed-form resistance equation from a governed literature dataset, reducing 497 raw records from 41 source blocks to 443 useable records from 37 sources through duplicate removal, governed density completion, deep-penetration filtering, and descriptor-only anomaly screening. Forrestal inversion maps each measured penetration depth to an operator-consistent effective resistance target described by mechanics-informed dimensionless descriptors. The artificial-intelligence contribution is a constrained equation-discovery workflow in which a categorical gradient-boosting model learns the nonlinear resistance surface, Shapley additive explanations restrict the analytical term family, and limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno optimization with bound constraints identifies equation coefficients under a forward penetration-depth objective. The engineering contribution is a 16-term explicit resistance law that replaces the empirical resistance relation inside the Forrestal operator while retaining its deterministic calculation form. On the 89-record held-out set, the equation gives a coefficient of determination of 0.9543 and a mean absolute percentage error of 14.88%, compared with 0.9206 and 24.44% for classical Forrestal and 0.9551 and 13.95% for the nonlinear resistance-reference model; its mean prediction-to-measurement ratio is 0.984. Repeated random, source-grouped, strength-stratified, out-of-distribution, input-uncertainty, and density-robustness tests bound the useable domain. The 80–120 MPa interval remains cautionary because of weaker held-out accuracy and limited cross-source support.

title: Energy-efficient deep learning-based vibration monitoring on parallel ultra-low-power microcontrollers
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) through vibration analysis is essential for ensuring safety, reliability, and minimized maintenance costs in sensor-connected environments. Realizing this at the extreme edge, directly on sensor nodes, requires advanced data analytics, ultra-energy-efficient hardware, and high-fidelity datasets. This paper addresses these challenges by developing an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based deep learning framework for vibration-based structural health monitoring tailored to resource-constrained devices. We present a benchmarking dataset for vibration SHM, encompassing nine abnormal conditions that capture narrowband structural anomalies. Leveraging this dataset, we design supervised and unsupervised deep-learning models, integrating a system identification (SysId) preprocessing stage to derive structurally informed features that enhance model input quality. This improves algorithmic results while boosting hardware performances. These models are deployed on a parallel ultra-low-power microcontroller with dedicated hardware acceleration. Our unsupervised anomaly detectors deliver 89.90 percent (%) accuracy, 4.1 percentage points higher than the state-of-the-art attention-based baseline, favoring recall and missed-detection reduction at the cost of a higher false-alarm rate while consuming 13 microjoules (µJ) in low-power mode and requiring 370 microseconds (µs) in high-performance mode. This marks one of the first experimental validations of unsupervised on-device vibration diagnostics. Supervised counterparts achieve 96.06 % binary and 91.5 % multiclass accuracy, rivaling Residual Network (ResNet) with 1 5 . 8 × fewer parameters, at less than 235 µJ and not more than 6.3 ms (ms) inference. Relative to existing edge implementations, our approach is one to three orders of magnitude more energy-efficient and two orders faster, unlocking AI-enabled autonomous, low-latency predictive maintenance for large-scale distributed infrastructure monitoring.

title: Multi-objective optimized signal decomposition with explainable and reliable hybrid models for multistep significant wave height forecasting in ocean wave energy applications
abstract: Accurate forecasting of significant wave height (Hs) is vital for marine safety, coastal engineering, and renewable energy production. This study presents an effective integrated model system to forecast Hs for two distinct sites in Australia, Gladstone and Palm Beach, over various time horizons from 30-min to 24-h ahead during the period of 2018 to 2022. In the first stage, a novel multi-objective Optuna is developed to optimize the decomposition parameters using two criteria of compactness, bandwidth, and peakedness of a signal's frequency spectrum. The proposed methodology is utilized for hyperparameter tuning of Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) and De-mixing Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition (D-MVMD) techniques. This enables an optimal data decomposition process by eliminating the need for manual parameter selection. In the second stage, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) approach, SHAPley Additive Explanations (SHAP), is used to identify the most influential components and analyze their interactions. These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to standalone forecasting models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). These optimized and interpretable decomposed signals are then used as inputs to the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), deep Random Vector Functional Link (RVFL), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models to forecast. In the final stage, a comprehensive Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS) is employed to quantify uncertainties and perform reliability analysis. The SHAP-based feature selection reduced the input variables from 37 to 48 decomposed components to a single dominant predictor while maintaining nearly identical predictive accuracy across all forecast horizons, significantly lowering computational costs. Among the models, the SSA-RVFL demonstrated superior performance, with lower computational cost and the highest forecasting accuracy across all time horizons. This model achieved the highest Index of Agreement (IA: 0.81-1) and determination coefficient (R 2 : 0.49-0.98), and lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE: 0.04-0.33) across stations and horizons. In addition, the results confirm operational reliability exceeding 88% for forecasts up to 6 h ahead. Overall, the fully optimized SSA integrated with the SHAP-RVFL-MCS results provides a robust framework for enhancing decision-making in coastal hazard and wave energy planning.
